```text
# Herdr: Tool Overview

## What It Is
Herdr is a **terminal multiplexer and agent orchestrator** built in **Rust**. It's designed specifically to manage AI coding agents alongside traditional terminal work within your existing terminal environment.

## How It Compares
| Feature | Herdr | tmux | GUI Managers |
|---------|-------|------|--------------|
| Persistent sessions | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Detach/reattach | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Agent awareness | ✓ | — | ✓ |
| Terminal-native | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Mouse support | ✓ | — | ✓ |

The creators position herdr as bridging tmux's persistence with GUI managers' agent awareness, staying "in your terminal" rather than opening separate applications.

## Key Features
- **Workspaces, tabs, and panes** with mouse-native interaction
- **Agent state detection** (blocked 🔴, working 🟡, done 🔵, idle 🟢)
- **Session persistence** with detach/reattach across restarts
- **18 built-in themes** (Catppuccin, Tokyo Night, Gruvbox, Rosé Pine, etc.)
- **Real terminal views** showing actual process output, not wrapped interpretations
- **Copy-friendly** pane selection with drag, double-click, or keyboard mode (`prefix+[`)

## Sessions/Windows/Panes Architecture
- **Sessions**: Named server instances managing separate runtime state
- **Workspaces**: Project-level containers within a session
- **Tabs**: Groups of panes within workspaces
- **Panes**: Real terminal processes that survive client detachment

## Keybindings & Configuration
Configuration uses **TOML** format at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`. Default prefix is `ctrl+b`:
- `prefix+c` — new tab
- `prefix+v` / `prefix+-` — split pane
- `prefix+z` — zoom pane
- `prefix+w` — workspace navigation
- Direct shortcuts like `ctrl+alt+n` bypass the prefix

## Agent Integration
Supports 15+ agents (Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Cursor, etc.) through:
- **Automatic detection** via process names and terminal output heuristics
- **Direct integrations** providing session identity and native state reporting
- **Socket API** allowing agents to create workspaces, manipulate panes, and respond to state changes

## Plugin/Extension System
Herdr provides a **Socket API** (documented in `/SKILL.md`) enabling agents to programmatically control workspaces and read terminal state. No traditional plugin system; instead, agents integrate via Unix sockets.

## Notable Limitations
- Windows support is "preview beta" only
- Agent state detection relies on heuristics without integration (no universal agent protocol)
- Limited to single-machine operation (no distributed agent support)
```
</details></tool-use>

2	# Theme-agnostic settings: plugins, general options, terminal compatibility.

13	# Session management

15	set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-continuum'
16	set -g @continuum-restore 'on'
17	
18	# Restore extra processes beyond resurrect's defaults (vim/nvim/emacs/less/...).
19	# Coding-agent CLIs and TUI tools are NOT in the default list, so without this
20	# they'd come back as a bare shell prompt at the right cwd. Adding them here
21	# makes resurrect re-exec the bare command (no args, no session resume — see
22	# pitfalls/tmux-resurrect-agents.md for why and what's lost).
23	set -g @resurrect-processes 'opencode claude codex aider gemini lazygit btop htop k9s lazydocker glow'
24	
25	# Floating scratch pane (prefix + F to toggle, prefix + P for menu)
26	set -g @plugin 'omerxx/tmux-floax'
27	set -g @floax-bind 'F'
28	set -g @floax-bind-menu 'P'
29	set -g @floax-width '80%'
30	set -g @floax-height '80%'
31	set -g @floax-border-color 'magenta'
32	set -g @floax-text-color 'blue'
33	set -g @floax-session-name 'float'
34	set -g @floax-change-path 'true'
35	
36	# URL picker: prefix + u opens fzf popup with all URLs in the pane
37	set -g @plugin 'joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url'
38	
39	# Open highlighted selection in copy-mode: o = open, C-o = open in $EDITOR, S = search
40	set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-open'
41	set -g @open-S 'https://www.google.com/search?q='
42	
43	# tmux-fzf: replaces the ugly built-in `prefix + ?` (list-keys dump) with an
44	# fzf popup over EVERY binding (incl. user-defined), plus session/window/pane/
45	# command/process/clipboard pickers. The plugin's launch key defaults to `F`
46	# which collides with tmux-floax — set it to `M-Z` (an unused key) so the
47	# plugin's auto-binding doesn't shadow floax. Our real entry point is
48	# `prefix + ?` (rebound in keybindings.conf).
49	# NOTE: `TMUX_FZF_LAUNCH_KEY=""` does NOT disable the auto-bind — the
50	# plugin's `[ -z "$VAR" ]` check treats empty as unset and falls back to `F`.
51	set -g @plugin 'sainnhe/tmux-fzf'
52	TMUX_FZF_LAUNCH_KEY="M-Z"
53	TMUX_FZF_OPTIONS="-p -w 80% -h 70% -m"
54	TMUX_FZF_ORDER="keybinding|session|window|pane|command|process|clipboard"
55	TMUX_FZF_PREVIEW=1
56	
57	# =============================================================================
58	# General Settings
59	# =============================================================================
60	
61	# No ESC delay (critical for Neovim and coding agents)
62	set -sg escape-time 0
63	
64	# Enable mouse support
65	setw -g mouse on
66	
67	# Use vi mode keys in copy mode (gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode` —
68	# default true; false → emacs copy-mode keymap. See docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md.)
69	setw -g mode-keys {{ if .enableVimMode }}vi{{ else }}emacs{{ end }}
70	
71	# Larger scrollback buffer
72	set -g history-limit 50000
73	
74	# Don't push the pre-clear screen contents into scrollback when a TUI issues a
75	# full-screen clear (ED). Streaming coding agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, etc.)
76	# that run on the main screen (not alternate-screen) otherwise leave ghost
77	# frames in history every repaint. Alt-screen apps (vim, htop) are unaffected.
78	# Default in tmux 3.3+ is `on`; we explicitly turn it off for cleaner scrollback.
79	# See pitfalls/tmux-scrollback-tui-repaint-ghosting.md.
80	set -g scroll-on-clear off
81	
82	# 1-indexed windows and panes
83	set -g base-index 1
84	setw -g pane-base-index 1
85	set -g renumber-windows on
86	
87	# Focus events for Vim autoread compatibility
88	set -g focus-events on
89	
90	# If the current session is destroyed, switch to another one instead of detaching
91	set -g detach-on-destroy off
92	
93	# Status bar visibility (position is set per-theme)
94	set-option -g status on
95	
96	# Window activity / silence / bell flags
97	# These drive the per-window flag glyphs (`#` activity, `~` silence, `!` bell)
98	# that Catppuccin's `window-status-format` already includes via #{window_flags}.
99	# Use case: glance at the tab bar to see which non-current window produced
100	# output (`#`) or has been quiet for a while (`~`). Useful for long builds /
101	# tests / pueue queues running in background panes.
102	#
103	# Limitation for LLM agent panes: opencode/claude run a spinner while the
104	# model is thinking, so from tmux's POV the pane is *always* active —
105	# `monitor-silence` will not fire for "agent waiting on user". For true
106	# semantic state (running / idle / error) on agent panes, see
107	# backlog/tmux-window-status-indicators.md.
108	#
109	# `visual-*` are kept off so the message line never spams; the flag in the
110	# tab list is the only visible signal.
111	setw -g monitor-activity on
112	setw -g monitor-bell on
113	setw -g monitor-silence 0
114	set -g visual-activity off
115	set -g visual-silence off
116	set -g visual-bell off
117	
118	# Status-bar messages (display-message) — default 750ms is too short to read
119	# multi-word confirmations like "Moved to foo:3 (zsh)" before they vanish.
120	# 0 = stay until the next key event (the key still does its normal action;
121	# only the message gets cleared). Trade-off: occasionally a stale message
122	# lingers if you stop typing, but no important confirmation is ever missed.
123	set -g display-time 0
124	
125	# =============================================================================
126	# Terminal & Key Compatibility
127	# =============================================================================
128	
129	set -s default-terminal 'tmux-256color'
130	set -as terminal-features ",xterm-256color:RGB"
131	
132	# Forward extended keys (CSI-u) so Ctrl+/, Shift+Enter etc. reach TUIs.
133	#
134	# Use `on` (NOT `always`):
135	#   - `on`: emit CSI-u only when a key has NO legacy encoding (Shift+Enter,
136	#     Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit). Keys with legacy encoding (Ctrl+letter
137	#     including Ctrl+J = LF, Ctrl+M = CR, Ctrl+I = TAB) keep their classic
138	#     bytes.
139	#   - `always`: emit CSI-u for EVERY modifier+key combo, including ones with
140	#     a legacy encoding. This breaks ble.sh paste handling because each `\n`
141	#     in pasted content gets re-encoded as `ESC[106;5u` (Ctrl+J as CSI-u),
142	#     and ble.sh inserts the escape sequence as literal text instead of as
143	#     a newline. See pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md.
144	#
145	# Net result on `on`: TUIs that need Ctrl+Enter / Shift+Enter (Claude Code,
146	# Neovim, etc.) still get them; paste of multi-line text into ble.sh works
147	# correctly; legacy `Ctrl+letter` shortcuts in shells / tmux / TUIs keep
148	# their normal encodings.
149	set -s extended-keys on
150	if-shell 'tmux -V | grep -qE "tmux ([3-9]\.[5-9]|[3-9]\.[1-9][0-9]|[4-9]\.)"' \
151	  'set -s extended-keys-format csi-u'
152	set -as terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'
153	
154	# OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)
155	set -g set-clipboard on
156	
157	# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
158	# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
159	# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these
160	# hints tmux falls back to terminfo's `Ms` capability, which is absent from
161	# the `tmux-256color` entry shipped by many distros, so yanks from inner
162	# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.
163	set -as terminal-features ",xterm*:clipboard"
164	set -as terminal-features ",ghostty*:clipboard"
165	set -as terminal-features ",alacritty*:clipboard"
166	
167	# Allow OSC passthrough (for terminal images, sixel, etc.)
168	set -g allow-passthrough on
169

28	| chezmoi-apply reload hint: `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_99_signal_reload.sh.tmpl` (touches sentinel) ↔ `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh` (reads sentinel + zsh/bash hook registration + `cas`/`cau` wrappers) | Row in [docs/shells/aliases.md](docs/shells/aliases.md) "Dotfiles management" section for `cas`/`cau` | The sentinel path `~/.cache/chezmoi/last-apply` is hard-coded in **two** places — the run-script that touches it and the shared backend that reads it. Keep both in sync when relocating (e.g. switching to `$XDG_STATE_HOME`). Hook registration is in the shared backend (NOT `dot_config/{zsh,bash}/99_*`) because bash's `$BASH_CONFIG_DIR` loads before `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell` (oh-my-bash `plugins=()` prereq, see `dot_bashrc.tmpl:94` vs `:114`), so a per-shell hook file in `dot_config/bash/` would run before the backend function exists. Opt out: `export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0`. |
29	| `app-*` helpers — `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` (macOS) ↔ `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` (Linux) ↔ `dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl` ↔ `dot_config/television/cable/linux-apps.toml.tmpl` | Both shell helpers MUST expose the SAME public verb names (`appquit` / `applaunch` / `appactivate` / `apprestart` / `apprunning` / `applist` / `appresponsive`) so users get cross-platform muscle memory. Backends diverge by necessity (Apple Events vs `gtk-launch` + `pkill -TERM` + optional GNOME `window-calls` ext). Adding a new verb to one side: decide whether it can also be implemented on the other; if not, document the gap in `backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md` "Open follow-ups". Both `tv` channel files MUST share Alt-key bindings where the verb exists on both sides — **Alt+H is mac-only by design** (Linux can't hide windows without compositor IPC; the Alt+H slot stays free on `tv linux-apps`). Per-app overrides for Linux AppImage/Snap/Flatpak runtime paths live in `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` (not auto-stubbed, matches `.shellrc.secrets` rule) — never auto-generate this file from the helper. | [docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md](docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md) "Controlling installed apps from the shell" section; [pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md](pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md), [pitfalls/linux-app-control-gapplication-zero-coverage.md](pitfalls/linux-app-control-gapplication-zero-coverage.md). Empirical baseline: `gapplication list-apps` returns only ~13 GNOME-core apps on Ubuntu 24.04 Wayland — third-party Electron/AppImage/Snap/Flatpak coverage is **zero**, so don't reach for `gapplication action … quit` as the primary mechanism. |
30	
31	**Repo-root files that stay OUT of MkDocs nav** (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md`, `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, `NOTES.md`): referenced via absolute GitHub URLs from [`docs/for-maintainers.md`](docs/for-maintainers.md), never copied via `pymdownx.snippets`.
32	
33	**Three-tier file placement** for new shell helpers:
34	
35	| Tier | Dir | When |
36	|---|---|---|
37	| Shared | `dot_config/shell/` | POSIX subset, both shells source. `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION` source-time dispatch is OK; ZLE widgets / `compdef` / `bindkey` / `setopt` / `read -q` / `${m:t}` / glob qualifiers are NOT (bash would error on source). |
38	| Zsh-only | `dot_config/zsh/` | ZLE widgets, `compdef`, `bindkey`, `setopt`, zsh-vi-mode hooks. |
39	| Bash-only | `dot_config/bash/` | `bind -x` / `ble-bind`, OMB plugin arrays, bash-specific `shopt`s. |
40	
41	When porting a zsh-only helper to bash via ble.sh, extract the shell-agnostic backend into `dot_config/shell/` and keep each shell's widget binding in its own dir.

43	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
44	
45	Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
46	
47	1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
48	2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
49	3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
50	4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
51	5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
52	6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers
53	
54	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.
55	
56	### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill
57	
58	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply` via `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`; see [docs/tools/agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template, disambiguation table, and upgrade path.
59	
60	**Fallback rules** so this section still binds when the skill cannot be loaded:
61	
62	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (priority/effort tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (research/design notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
63	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
64	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
65	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it (a) recurs across machines, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.
66	
67	## Chezmoi templating conventions
68	
69	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
70	
71	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
72	
73	| Predicate | Use |
74	|---|---|
75	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
76	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
77	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
78	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
79	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |
80	
81	Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
82	
83	## Hard repo invariants
84	
85	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
86	
87	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
88	
89	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
90	
91	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
92	
93	**Hard rules**:
94	
95	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
96	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
97	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
98	
99	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
100	
101	### Three-tier user-local override layer
102	
103	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
104	
105	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
106	
107	```
108	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
109	```
110	
111	Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
112	
113	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
114	
115	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
116	
117	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 2 first-seed files (`marimo.toml`, btop's `btop.conf`): [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
118	
119	**Hard rules**:
120	
121	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
122	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
123	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
124	- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
125	- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
126	
127	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
128	
129	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
130	
131	**Hard rules**:
132	
133	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
134	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
135	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a single tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it legitimately needs a newer version (e.g. `python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5` for `--with-executables-from`). MUST detect install style (brew vs curl/standalone) and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors if not a brew formula). Dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`. See [docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
136	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`. Without it the install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already exists, and entry-point shims are never written (silent missing `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit: `yq '.python_uv_tools[] | select(.with_executables_from) | select(.extra_binaries == null) | .name' …` MUST print nothing. See [pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
137	- New upgrade category: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md → Adding a new category](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). For a tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise: do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
138	
139	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
140	
141	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
142	
143	**Hard rules**:
144	
145	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
146	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
147	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
148	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
149	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
150	
151	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**:
152	
153	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
154	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag.
155	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
156	4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.
157	
158	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
159	
160	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
161	
162	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
163	
164	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
165	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
166	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
167	- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
168	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
169	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
170	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
171	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
172	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
173	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
174	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
175	
176	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
177	
178	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
179	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
180	
181	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
182	
183	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
184	
185	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
186	
187	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
188	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
189	
190	**Hard rules**:
191	
192	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
193	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
194	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
195	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
196	
197	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
198	
199	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
200	
201	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
202	
203	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
204	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
205	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
206	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.

152	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
153	# Command-boundary navigation in copy-mode (Warp-style).
154	# Requires OSC 133 markers from the shell — emitted by
155	# dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh. In a plain shell (no markers,
156	# e.g. `sh`, `bash` without our hook, or `DISABLE_OSC133=1`), these keys are
157	# no-ops. tmux 3.4+ required for next-prompt/previous-prompt; the `-o` variant
158	# (jump to output start, not prompt start) is tmux 3.5+.
159	#
160	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
161	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
162	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
163	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
164	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
165	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
166	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o
167	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o

173	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard
174	# `load-buffer -w -` loads into tmux's paste buffer AND forwards to the outer
175	# terminal via OSC 52 (requires `set-clipboard on` in common.conf). This works
176	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
177	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"

179	# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard

183	bind C-y run-shell "\
184	  tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort \
185	    --header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)' \
186	    | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"
187	
188	# prefix + M-y: copy the LAST command's OUTPUT to clipboard (Warp-style).
189	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,
190	# DISABLE_OSC133=1, or a remote bash without our hook), selection ends up
191	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
192	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
193	# flash confirmation.
194	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
195	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
196	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
197	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
198	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \

204	# not just "echo hi"). Trim in the paste target if needed. Chain: enter
205	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
206	# forward to the C marker (= start of output = end of input line), copy.
207	bind M-i copy-mode \; \
208	  send-keys -X previous-prompt \; \
209	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \

1	# ~/.config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh
2	# Source: dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh (managed by chezmoi)
3	#
4	# Generic per-window tmux status badge helpers — POSIX, sourced by both
5	# zsh and bash. Thin convenience layer over the same primitive workmux
6	# uses (`tmux set-option -w '@<name>_status' '<glyph>'`), so any script /
7	# hook / cron job / build watcher can tag its tmux window without
8	# pulling in workmux.
9	#
10	# Why a shared layer (not in 38_workmux.zsh): these helpers don't need
11	# any zsh feature, and the most common consumers (build scripts, deploy
12	# hooks, CI wrappers) tend to be `#!/bin/bash` or `#!/bin/sh`. Putting
13	# them in dot_config/shell/ means they Just Work from any shell.
14	#
15	# Companion: docs/tools/workmux.md → "Reusing the per-window status
16	# mechanism (without workmux)" for design rationale, the lifecycle hard
17	# rules, and the build-watcher worked example.
18	#
19	# Quick reference:
20	#
21	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨           # tag current window
22	#   tmux_status_set my_build 🔨 mysess:3  # tag specific window
23	#   tmux_status_get my_build              # read current window
24	#   tmux_status_clear my_build            # unset (current window)
25	#   tmux_status_clear my_build mysess:3   # unset specific window
26	#   tmux_status_clear_all my_build        # unset across every session
27	#   tmux_status_list                      # list every @*_status user-var
28	#   tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
29	#                                         # set 🔨, run cmd, set ✅/❌
30	#                                         # by exit code, auto-clear on
31	#                                         # signal trap
32	#
33	# Naming convention: pass the LOGICAL name without `@` or `_status`
34	# suffix — these helpers add the `@<name>_status` wrapper. So
35	# `tmux_status_set my_build 🔨` writes `@my_build_status`. This keeps
36	# the user-var namespace tidy (`@<tool>_status` everywhere) and lets
37	# you grep for "every status producer" with `tmux_status_list`.
38	
39	# Skip silently if tmux isn't on PATH (cron, headless SSH, fresh box
40	# pre-ansible). Producers can call these unconditionally.
41	command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0
42	
43	# Internal: validate name (alphanumeric + underscore + dash, no `@` /
44	# `_status` since we add them). Returns 0 if valid, 1 if not (with
45	# stderr diagnostic). Empty name is rejected. Names starting with
46	# `workmux` are reserved to avoid clobbering workmux's own user-var.
47	_tmux_status_validate_name() {
48	    if [ -z "${1:-}" ]; then
49	        printf 'tmux_status: name argument is required\n' >&2
50	        return 1
51	    fi
52	    case "$1" in
53	        workmux*)
54	            # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks here are literal Markdown-style code spans, not command substitution.
55	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" reserved (workmux owns @workmux_status). Use `workmux set-window-status` for the agent path.\n' "$1" >&2
56	            return 1
57	            ;;
58	        *[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*)
59	            printf 'tmux_status: name "%s" must be [A-Za-z0-9_-]+\n' "$1" >&2
60	            return 1
61	            ;;
62	    esac
63	    return 0
64	}
65	
66	# tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]
67	#   target defaults to current window (`tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}'`)
68	tmux_status_set() {
69	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
70	    if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then
71	        printf 'tmux_status_set: usage: tmux_status_set <name> <glyph> [target]\n' >&2
72	        return 1
73	    fi
74	    _name="$1"
75	    _glyph="$2"
76	    _target="${3:-}"
77	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
78	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph" 2>/dev/null
79	    else
80	        tmux set-option -w "@${_name}_status" "$_glyph" 2>/dev/null
81	    fi
82	}
83	
84	# tmux_status_get <name> [target]
85	#   prints the glyph (or empty string + non-zero exit if unset)
86	tmux_status_get() {
87	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
88	    _name="$1"
89	    _target="${2:-}"
90	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
91	        tmux show-options -wv -t "$_target" "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
92	    else
93	        tmux show-options -wv "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
94	    fi
95	}
96	
97	# tmux_status_clear <name> [target]
98	tmux_status_clear() {
99	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
100	    _name="$1"
101	    _target="${2:-}"
102	    if [ -n "$_target" ]; then
103	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_target" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
104	    else
105	        tmux set-option -w -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
106	    fi
107	}
108	
109	# tmux_status_clear_all <name>
110	#   walk every window in every session, unset @<name>_status
111	tmux_status_clear_all() {
112	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
113	    _name="$1"
114	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _w; do
115	        tmux set-option -w -t "$_w" -u "@${_name}_status" 2>/dev/null
116	    done
117	}
118	
119	# tmux_status_list
120	#   show every @*_status user-var across every window (read-only audit)
121	tmux_status_list() {
122	    tmux list-windows -aF '#{session_name}:#{window_index} #{window_name}' 2>/dev/null | while IFS= read -r _line; do
123	        _w="${_line%% *}"
124	        # Pull every option starting with @ on this window, filter to *_status
125	        tmux show-options -w -t "$_w" 2>/dev/null \
126	            | awk -v w="$_line" '/^@[A-Za-z0-9_-]+_status / {print w "  " $0}'
127	    done
128	}
129	
130	# tmux_status_run <name> <working_glyph> <ok_glyph> <fail_glyph> -- <cmd> [args...]
131	#   Run a command, badge the window with `working_glyph` while it runs,
132	#   then `ok_glyph` on success or `fail_glyph` on failure. Traps INT /
133	#   TERM / HUP to clear the badge instead of leaking on Ctrl+C.
134	#
135	#   Example:
136	#     tmux_status_run my_build 🔨 ✅ ❌ -- npm run build
137	#     tmux_status_run deploy   🚀 🟢 🔴 -- ./deploy.sh prod
138	tmux_status_run() {
139	    _tmux_status_validate_name "${1:-}" || return 1
140	    if [ $# -lt 6 ]; then
141	        printf 'tmux_status_run: usage: tmux_status_run <name> <working> <ok> <fail> -- <cmd> [args...]\n' >&2
142	        return 1
143	    fi
144	    _name="$1"
145	    _working="$2"
146	    _ok="$3"
147	    _fail="$4"
148	    shift 4
149	    if [ "${1:-}" != "--" ]; then
150	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
151	        printf 'tmux_status_run: missing `--` separator before command\n' >&2
152	        return 1
153	    fi
154	    shift
155	    if [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
156	        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # Backticks are literal in the diagnostic message.
157	        printf 'tmux_status_run: no command after `--`\n' >&2
158	        return 1
159	    fi
160	
161	    # Capture target ONCE up front — if `cmd` happens to switch tmux
162	    # window, we still want the badge to land on the window the user
163	    # invoked from.
164	    _target=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}:#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
165	    [ -z "$_target" ] && _target=""
166	
167	    # Trap so Ctrl+C / kill doesn't leak the working glyph forever.
168	    # Use a trap that clears, then re-raises the signal default for
169	    # correct exit semantics.
170	    trap '_tmux_status_run_trap "$_name" "$_target"' INT TERM HUP
171	
172	    tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_working" "$_target"
173	    "$@"
174	    _rc=$?
175	    if [ $_rc -eq 0 ]; then
176	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_ok" "$_target"
177	    else
178	        tmux_status_set "$_name" "$_fail" "$_target"
179	    fi
180	
181	    trap - INT TERM HUP
182	    return $_rc
183	}
184	
185	# Internal: trap helper for tmux_status_run. Clears the badge then
186	# re-raises the signal so the calling shell sees correct $? / exit code.
187	_tmux_status_run_trap() {
188	    tmux_status_clear "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null
189	    trap - INT TERM HUP
190	    # Re-raise INT (most common case); for TERM/HUP we just let the
191	    # shell continue — calling scripts can decide what to do via $?.
192	    kill -INT $$ 2>/dev/null
193	}
194

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Top-level tmux popup menu — invoked by `prefix + Space`.
3	#
4	# Why a script (not inline `display-menu` in keybindings.conf):
5	#   1. tmux's command parser stops at literal `;`, `{`, `}` even inside
6	#      nested quotes. With ~50 menu rows full of fzf binds and shell
7	#      one-liners, escaping became fragile and broke silently.
8	#   2. tmux `display-menu` does not paginate. If the menu is taller than
9	#      the terminal, the entire popup is suppressed with no error. By
10	#      generating the menu here we can read $TMUX client_height and
11	#      auto-trim low-frequency rows when small.
12	#   3. Submenus are normal `tmux display-menu` invocations from rows;
13	#      they don't share quoting context with the parent menu.
14	#
15	# Submenus live in sibling scripts:
16	#   menu-layouts.sh, menu-session.sh, menu-sesh.sh,
17	#   menu-popups.sh, menu-theme.sh, menu-system.sh, menu-agents.sh
18	#
19	# See: pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-parse-failure.md
20	
21	set -euo pipefail
22	
23	H=$(tmux display-message -p '#{client_height}')
24	DIR=~/.config/tmux
25	
26	# Tier 0: ALWAYS shown (highest frequency, ~7 rows + 2 separators)
27	declare -a tier0=(
28	  "Last window"  Tab "last-window"
29	  "Last pane"    P   "last-pane"
30	  ""             ""  ""
31	  "Choose win"   w   "choose-tree -Zw"
32	  "Choose sess"  s   "choose-tree -Zs"
33	  "Pane #s"      q   "display-panes -d 0"
34	  ""             ""  ""
35	  "Sesh picker"  g   "run-shell '$DIR/sesh-picker.sh'"
36	  "Lazygit"      G   "display-popup -E -w 90% -h 90% -d '#{pane_current_path}' -T ' lazygit ' 'lazygit'"
37	)
38	
39	# Tier 1: shown when height >= 22 (adds new-window/split/zoom)
40	declare -a tier1=(
41	  ""             ""  ""
42	  "New window"   c   "new-window -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
43	  "Split |"      "|" "split-window -h -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
44	  "Split -"      "-" "split-window -v -c '#{pane_current_path}'"
45	  "Zoom"         z   "resize-pane -Z"
46	)
47	
48	# Tier 2: submenus + cheatsheet (always shown if Tier 1 is shown)
49	declare -a tier2=(
50	  ""             ""  ""
51	  "→ Layouts"    L   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-layouts.sh'"
52	  "→ Session"    S   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-session.sh'"
53	  "→ Sesh+"      E   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-sesh.sh'"
54	  "→ Agents"     A   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-agents.sh'"
55	  "→ Popups"     o   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-popups.sh'"
56	  "→ Theme"      T   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-theme.sh'"
57	  "→ System"     Y   "run-shell '$DIR/menu-system.sh'"
58	  ""             ""  ""
59	  "Cheatsheet"   "?" "display-popup -E -w 80% -h 80% -T ' tmux cheatsheet ' 'glow -p $DIR/cheatsheet.md 2>/dev/null || less $DIR/cheatsheet.md'"
60	  "Search keys"  "/" "run-shell -b ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf/scripts/keybinding.sh"
61	)
62	
63	rows=("${tier0[@]}")
64	if [ "$H" -ge 22 ]; then
65	  rows+=("${tier1[@]}" "${tier2[@]}")
66	elif [ "$H" -ge 14 ]; then
67	  rows+=("${tier2[@]}")
68	fi
69	
70	exec tmux display-menu -T "#[align=centre,bold]tmux (h=$H)" -x R -y P "${rows[@]}"

1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: hook-aware deep-merge of a managed overlay into
3	# ~/.claude/settings.json.
4	#
5	# Why hook-aware? Claude Code rewrites this file at runtime AND CodeIsland
6	# (https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland, macOS notch HUD) auto-installs its
7	# own entries into hooks.Notification / hooks.PermissionRequest / hooks.Stop
8	# / hooks.PreToolUse / etc. workmux's `wm setup` ALSO writes Stop /
9	# UserPromptSubmit / Notification hook entries (see docs/tools/workmux.md
10	# → "Claude leak"). A naive `jq '. * $overlay'` deep-merge replaces arrays
11	# wholesale, so declaring our notify.sh hook in the overlay would silently
12	# delete every CodeIsland / workmux entry on each `chezmoi apply` (and the
13	# tools would re-install on next launch — endless ping-pong).
14	#
15	# How: For all keys EXCEPT .hooks, do the normal recursive object merge.
16	# For .hooks.<event> arrays, additively merge — append overlay entries that
17	# aren't already present (matched by .hooks[0].command), preserving every
18	# entry the live file already contains. This lets our overlay enforce
19	# notify.sh + workmux status updates while CodeIsland / workmux setup /
20	# any other tool freely manage their own parallel entries in the same
21	# event arrays.
22	#
23	# Workmux integration: We declare the workmux Stop / SubagentStop /
24	# UserPromptSubmit / Notification hooks here directly so they're enforced
25	# on every chezmoi apply WITHOUT requiring users to also run `wm setup`.
26	# The `command -v workmux` guard lets the hook no-op silently on machines
27	# where workmux isn't installed yet (fresh box, Linux without ansible run,
28	# etc.). This patches Claude's by-design 🤖-leak: Anthropic's Stop hook
29	# fires on every turn end, but workmux's `working` state never auto-clears
30	# without an explicit `done` set.
31	#
32	# To manage an additional hook event: add it to $overlay.hooks below.
33	# To manage an additional non-hook key: add it to $overlay.
34	# Requires: jq (installed by the `base` ansible role). On a fresh-box first
35	# apply, jq isn't yet installed; this script falls back to passing the live
36	# file through unchanged. See pitfalls/modify-script-jq-bootstrap-cycle.md.
37	#
38	# See: docs/tools/agent-overlays.md → "CodeIsland integration".
39	set -eu
40	
41	overlay=$(cat <<'JSON'
42	{
43	  "hooks": {
44	    "Notification": [
45	      {
46	        "matcher": "",
47	        "hooks": [
48	          {
49	            "type": "command",
50	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
51	          }
52	        ]
53	      },
54	      {
55	        "matcher": "",
56	        "hooks": [
57	          {
58	            "type": "command",
59	            "command": "command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status waiting || true"
60	          }
61	        ]
62	      }
63	    ],
64	    "UserPromptSubmit": [
65	      {
66	        "matcher": "",
67	        "hooks": [
68	          {
69	            "type": "command",
70	            "command": "command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status working || true"
71	          }
72	        ]
73	      }
74	    ],
75	    "Stop": [
76	      {
77	        "hooks": [
78	          {
79	            "type": "command",
80	            "command": "~/.claude/hooks/notify.sh"
81	          }
82	        ]
83	      },
84	      {
85	        "hooks": [
86	          {
87	            "type": "command",
88	            "command": "command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status done || true"
89	          }
90	        ]
91	      }
92	    ],
93	    "SubagentStop": [
94	      {
95	        "hooks": [
96	          {
97	            "type": "command",
98	            "command": "command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && workmux set-window-status done || true"
99	          }
100	        ]
101	      }
102	    ]
103	  },
104	  "enabledPlugins": {
105	    "pyright-lsp@claude-plugins-official": true,
106	    "claude-hud@claude-hud": true
107	  },
108	  "extraKnownMarketplaces": {
109	    "claude-hud": {
110	      "source": {
111	        "source": "github",
112	        "repo": "jarrodwatts/claude-hud"
113	      }
114	    }
115	  },
116	  "skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt": true,
117	  "permissions": {
118	    "defaultMode": "bypassPermissions"
119	  },
120	  "statusLine": {
121	    "type": "command",
122	    "command": "bash -c 'plugin_dir=$(ls -d \"${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}\"/plugins/cache/claude-hud/claude-hud/*/ 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -1); runtime=$(command -v bun 2>/dev/null || command -v node 2>/dev/null); [ -z \"$runtime\" ] && exit 0; rt=\"${runtime##*/}\"; if [ \"$rt\" = \"bun\" ]; then exec \"$runtime\" --env-file /dev/null \"${plugin_dir}src/index.ts\"; else exec \"$runtime\" \"${plugin_dir}dist/index.js\"; fi'"
123	  }
124	}
125	JSON
126	)
127	
128	base=$(cat)
129	[ -z "$base" ] && base='{}'
130	
131	# Cold-start fallback: jq is installed by the `base` ansible role, which
132	# runs AFTER this file-apply phase. Pass the live file through unchanged
133	# and warn — the next apply (after ansible) does the real merge.
134	if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
135	  printf '%s\n' "modify_settings.json: jq not found; passing live file through unchanged. Re-run \`chezmoi apply\` after the base ansible role installs jq." >&2
136	  printf '%s' "$base"
137	  exit 0
138	fi
139	
140	# Hook-aware merge:
141	#   1. Compute non-hook portion of overlay (everything except .hooks).
142	#   2. Deep-merge that into base normally: base * overlay_no_hooks.
143	#   3. For each event in overlay.hooks, append entries whose .hooks[0].command
144	#      isn't already represented in the live event array (by exact-string
145	#      command match on .hooks[0].command). Live entries are preserved
146	#      verbatim, and new overlay entries are added at the end.
147	printf '%s' "$base" | jq --argjson overlay "$overlay" '
148	  . as $base
149	  | ($overlay | del(.hooks)) as $non_hook_overlay
150	  | ($overlay.hooks // {}) as $overlay_hooks
151	  | ($base * $non_hook_overlay) as $merged
152	  | $merged
153	  | .hooks = (
154	      ($merged.hooks // {}) as $live_hooks
155	      | reduce ($overlay_hooks | to_entries[]) as $ev (
156	          $live_hooks;
157	          .[$ev.key] = (
158	            (.[$ev.key] // []) as $live_arr
159	            | ($live_arr | map(.hooks[0].command? // "")) as $live_cmds
160	            | $live_arr + (
161	                $ev.value
162	                | map(select(
163	                    (.hooks[0].command? // "") as $cmd
164	                    | ($cmd == "") or (($live_cmds | index($cmd)) == null)
165	                  ))
166	              )
167	          )
168	        )
169	    )
170	'
171
