7	#   print -n                        → printf '%s'
8	#   frames[$(( (i%10)+1 ))]         → ${frames[*]:$(( i%10 )):1} (bash-style 0-idx slice)
9	#   ${pipestatus[1]}                → shell-dispatched ($PIPESTATUS[0] / $pipestatus[1])
10	#   &!                              → & disown
11	#   read -q "var?prompt"            → shell-dispatched (bash uses read -n 1 -p)
12	#   emulate -L zsh                  → gated on $ZSH_VERSION
13	#
14	# Depends on cpblock from dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh (still
15	# zsh-only — relies on ZLE BUFFER/POSTDISPLAY). In bash, `aifix`/`aiexplain`
16	# error out with a hint to use `aifix-stdin` / `aifix-run` / `aifix-rerun`
17	# which don't need cpblock.
18	#
19	#   aifix [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]
20	#   aiexplain [N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]
21	#   aiblock                                                    # Python TUI
22	#
23	# Agent auto-detection order and per-vendor lightweight model pins live in
24	# dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh (the SSOT, sourced at shell init). This
25	# file READS the resulting AICAP_* env vars; it does NOT define defaults.
26	# To change the autodetect order globally, edit AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY in the
27	# SSOT. To pin a different model for one tool, `export AICAP_<AGENT>_MODEL=…`
28	# before invoking it.
29	# Override via -a AGENT (per-call) or AICAP_AGENT env var (per-shell).
30	# Advisory-only by design; there is no --execute flag.
31	# For a back-and-forth interactive session, use `aiblock` → "Spawn agent".
32	#
33	# A fifth agent type `http` talks an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint
34	# directly via curl + jq. Use it for OpenRouter free models or local Ollama
35	# without depending on any agent CLI being installed:
36	#
37	#   AICAP_AGENT=http aifix              # OpenRouter (free Gemini Flash by default)
38	#   AICAP_AGENT=http \
39	#     AICAP_HTTP_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
40	#     AICAP_HTTP_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder:7b aifix
41	#
42	# `http` is opt-in: it is never auto-detected (nothing on PATH to probe).
43	#
44	# Env vars (set in ~/.shellrc.adhoc or ~/.config/{zsh/secrets.zsh,bash/secrets.sh}
45	# to override — those files always win against the SSOT's `: "${VAR:=…}"` defaults):
46	#
47	#   AICAP_AGENT            default: (unset — auto-detect via AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY)
48	#                                        force a specific agent: opencode | claude |
49	#                                        codex | agyc | cursor-agent | http
50	#   AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY   default: opencode claude codex agyc cursor-agent (SSOT)
51	#   AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL     default: haiku                                  (SSOT)
52	#   AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL   default: github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5        (SSOT)
53	#   AICAP_CODEX_MODEL      default: (unset — gpt-5-mini errors on ChatGPT auth) (SSOT)
54	#   AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL     default: (unset — let cursor-agent pick)        (SSOT)
55	#   AICAP_HTTP_URL         default: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions (SSOT)
56	#   AICAP_HTTP_MODEL       default: google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free        (SSOT)
57	#   AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY     default: $OPENROUTER_API_KEY (empty = no auth header)
58	#   AICAP_SHOW_METADATA    default: 1  (tokens / cost / model on stderr; this file only)
59	#   AICAP_PRETTIFY         default: 1  (auto: glow → bat → raw; non-tty = raw)
60	#   AICAP_SPINNER          default: 1  (braille on stderr while agent thinks)
61	#
62	# Vars marked (SSOT) live in dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh — change them
63	# there once, all four consumers (aifix, aiblock, aisuggest, tsum) see it.
64	
65	# Defensive load: if 04_ai_agents.sh wasn't sourced first (e.g. someone
66	# dot-sourced this file directly without running rc), pull it in now.
67	if [ -z "${_AICAP_AGENT_CONFIG_SOURCED:-}" ] && [ -r "$HOME/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh" ]; then
68	  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
69	  source "$HOME/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh"
70	fi
71	
72	# UX-only flags that don't apply to the Python consumers — these stay here.
73	: "${AICAP_SHOW_METADATA:=1}"
74	: "${AICAP_PRETTIFY:=1}"
75	: "${AICAP_SPINNER:=1}"
76	
77	_aiagent_autodetect() {
78	  local cand
79	  # Word-split $AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY. The original `${=…}` was zsh's explicit
80	  # word-splitting flag (zsh doesn't split unquoted params by default); bash
81	  # does auto-split unquoted. Dispatch:
82	  local _priority="${AICAP_AGENT_PRIORITY:-opencode claude codex cursor-agent}"
83	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
84	    setopt local_options sh_word_split
85	  fi
86	  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
87	  for cand in $_priority; do
88	    if command -v "$cand" &>/dev/null; then
89	      printf '%s\n' "$cand"
90	      return 0
91	    fi
92	  done
93	  return 1
94	}
95	
96	# Background spinner on stderr while the agent is thinking. Skipped when
97	# AICAP_SPINNER=0 or stderr isn't a tty (so pipes / file redirects stay
98	# clean). The spinner subprocess is disowned via `& disown` so it survives
99	# the command substitution that invokes the agent.
100	_AICAP_SPIN_PID=
101	_aicap_spinner_start() {
102	  [ "$AICAP_SPINNER" != "1" ] && return 0
103	  [ ! -t 2 ] && return 0
104	  local label="${1:-thinking}"
105	  (
106	    trap 'exit 0' TERM INT HUP
107	    local -a frames
108	    frames=('⠋' '⠙' '⠹' '⠸' '⠼' '⠴' '⠦' '⠧' '⠇' '⠏')
109	    local i=0
110	    while true; do
111	      # ${arr[*]:N:1} is bash-style array slicing (0-indexed); zsh supports
112	      # the same syntax. Quoted, a 1-element slice expands as one word.
113	      printf '\r\e[K%s %s' "${frames[*]:$(( i % 10 )):1}" "$label" >&2
114	      i=$(( i + 1 ))
115	      sleep 0.1
116	    done
117	  ) & disown
118	  _AICAP_SPIN_PID=$!
119	}
120	
121	_aicap_spinner_stop() {
122	  [ -z "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" ] && return 0
123	  kill "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" 2>/dev/null
124	  # Drain; both shells wait on PIDs even if disowned as long as we know the PID.
125	  wait "$_AICAP_SPIN_PID" 2>/dev/null
126	  _AICAP_SPIN_PID=
127	  [ -t 2 ] && printf '\r\e[K' >&2
128	}
129	
130	# Pretty-print stdin as Markdown: glow > bat > raw. Skips prettify if stdout
131	# is NOT a tty (so pipes stay clean) or AICAP_PRETTIFY=0.
132	_aicap_prettify() {
133	  if [ "$AICAP_PRETTIFY" != "1" ] || [ ! -t 1 ]; then
134	    cat
135	  elif command -v glow &>/dev/null; then
136	    glow -
137	  elif command -v bat &>/dev/null; then
138	    bat --language=md --style=plain --paging=never --color=always
139	  else
140	    cat
141	  fi
142	}
143	
144	# Invoke a coding-agent in one-shot mode.
145	#
146	# Writes reply (text) to stdout. Writes metadata line to stderr when
147	# AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=1 and the agent supports structured JSON output.
148	# Currently only Claude's JSON includes usage/cost — other agents just get a
149	# "<agent> (<model>)" line on stderr.
150	_aiagent_invoke() {
151	  local agent="$1" prompt="$2"
152	  local json reply model_used tokens_in tokens_out cache_read cache_create cost duration rc
153	
154	  # Ensure spinner cleans up if the caller returns or we hit a trap.
155	  trap '_aicap_spinner_stop' EXIT INT TERM
156	
157	  case "$agent" in
158	    claude)
159	      # Conditional --model: empty AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL → claude picks its
160	      # own default (robust if the pinned alias is ever retired).
161	      local -a claude_model_args
162	      claude_model_args=()
163	      [ -n "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL" ] && claude_model_args=(--model "$AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL")
164	      local claude_model_label="${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL:-(default)}"
165	      if [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" = "1" ] && command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
166	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $claude_model_label (json)…"
167	        json=$(claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" --output-format json "$prompt")
168	        rc=$?
169	        _aicap_spinner_stop
170	        (( rc != 0 )) && return $rc
171	        reply=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.result // empty')
172	        model_used=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.modelUsage | keys | first // "?"')
173	        tokens_in=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.input_tokens // "?"')
174	        tokens_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.output_tokens // "?"')
175	        cache_read=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_read_input_tokens // 0')
176	        cache_create=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.usage.cache_creation_input_tokens // 0')
177	        cost=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.total_cost_usd // "?"')
178	        duration=$(printf '%s\n' "$json" | jq -r '.duration_ms // "?"')
179	        printf '%s\n' "claude ($model_used) | in=$tokens_in out=$tokens_out cache=(r:$cache_read,w:$cache_create) | cost=\$$cost ${duration}ms" >&2
180	        printf '%s\n' "$reply"
181	      else
182	        printf '%s\n' "claude ($claude_model_label)" >&2
183	        _aicap_spinner_start "claude $claude_model_label…"
184	        claude -p "${claude_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
185	        rc=$?
186	        _aicap_spinner_stop
187	        return $rc
188	      fi
189	      ;;
190	    opencode)
191	      local -a opencode_model_args
192	      opencode_model_args=()
193	      [ -n "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL" ] && opencode_model_args=(-m "$AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL")
194	      local opencode_model_label="${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL:-(default)}"
195	      printf '%s\n' "opencode ($opencode_model_label)" >&2
196	      _aicap_spinner_start "opencode $opencode_model_label…"
197	      opencode run "${opencode_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
198	      rc=$?
199	      _aicap_spinner_stop
200	      return $rc
201	      ;;
202	    codex)
203	      # AICAP_CODEX_MODEL defaults to empty since gpt-5-mini is rejected on
204	      # ChatGPT-account auth. Users on API-key auth can re-pin via the env.
205	      local -a codex_model_args
206	      codex_model_args=()
207	      [ -n "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL" ] && codex_model_args=(-m "$AICAP_CODEX_MODEL")
208	      local codex_model_label="${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL:-(default)}"
209	      printf '%s\n' "codex ($codex_model_label)" >&2
210	      _aicap_spinner_start "codex $codex_model_label…"
211	      codex exec "${codex_model_args[@]}" "$prompt"
212	      rc=$?
213	      _aicap_spinner_stop
214	      return $rc
215	      ;;
216	    cursor-agent)
217	      if [ -n "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" ]; then
218	        printf '%s\n' "cursor-agent ($AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL)" >&2
219	        _aicap_spinner_start "cursor-agent $AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL…"
220	        cursor-agent -p --model "$AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL" "$prompt"
221	      else
222	        printf '%s\n' "cursor-agent" >&2
223	        _aicap_spinner_start "cursor-agent…"
224	        cursor-agent -p "$prompt"
225	      fi
226	      rc=$?
227	      _aicap_spinner_stop
228	      return $rc
229	      ;;
230	    agyc)
231	      # Antigravity CLI one-shot. Reached via the collision-free `agyc` symlink
232	      # (the IDE squats bare `agy`). No `--model` flag — model is account/config-side.
233	      printf '%s\n' "agyc (antigravity)" >&2
234	      _aicap_spinner_start "agyc…"
235	      agyc -p "$prompt"
236	      rc=$?
237	      _aicap_spinner_stop
238	      return $rc
239	      ;;
240	    http)
241	      # OpenAI-compatible chat-completions over curl. Covers OpenRouter (with
242	      # API key) and local Ollama (no auth) with the same code path. Never
243	      # auto-detected — opt in via AICAP_AGENT=http or `-a http`.
244	      local url="$AICAP_HTTP_URL" model="$AICAP_HTTP_MODEL"
245	      local key="${AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:-${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}}"
246	      if ! command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
247	        printf '%s\n' "aifix: jq is required for the http agent" >&2
248	        return 1
249	      fi
250	      if ! command -v curl &>/dev/null; then
251	        printf '%s\n' "aifix: curl is required for the http agent" >&2
252	        return 1
253	      fi
254	      # Extract host from URL. Original used zsh-nested `${${url#*://}%%/*}`;
255	      # bash doesn't support nested expansion, so do it in two steps.
256	      local host
257	      host="${url#*://}"
258	      host="${host%%/*}"
259	      [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" != "1" ] && printf '%s\n' "http ($model @ $host)" >&2
260	      _aicap_spinner_start "http $model…"
261	      local payload response
262	      payload=$(jq -n --arg m "$model" --arg p "$prompt" \
263	        '{model: $m, messages: [{role: "user", content: $p}], stream: false}')
264	      local -a curl_args
265	      curl_args=(-sS -X POST "$url" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$payload")
266	      [ -n "$key" ] && curl_args+=(-H "Authorization: Bearer $key")
267	      response=$(curl "${curl_args[@]}")
268	      rc=$?
269	      _aicap_spinner_stop
270	      if (( rc != 0 )); then
271	        printf '%s\n' "http: curl failed (rc=$rc) — check AICAP_HTTP_URL ($url)" >&2
272	        return $rc
273	      fi
274	      local err
275	      err=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.error.message // (.error | strings) // empty' 2>/dev/null)
276	      if [ -n "$err" ]; then
277	        printf '%s\n' "http: API error: $err" >&2
278	        return 1
279	      fi
280	      reply=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.choices[0].message.content // empty')
281	      if [ -z "$reply" ]; then
282	        printf '%s\n' "http: empty reply (raw response: $response)" >&2
283	        return 1
284	      fi
285	      if [ "$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" = "1" ]; then
286	        tokens_in=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.usage.prompt_tokens // "?"')
287	        tokens_out=$(printf '%s\n' "$response" | jq -r '.usage.completion_tokens // "?"')
288	        printf '%s\n' "http ($model @ $host) | in=$tokens_in out=$tokens_out" >&2
289	      fi
290	      printf '%s\n' "$reply"
291	      ;;
292	    *) printf '%s\n' "aifix: unknown agent '$agent' (supported: opencode, claude, codex, agyc, cursor-agent, http)" >&2; return 1 ;;
293	  esac
294	}
295	
296	# Core dispatcher: given an already-captured block, build the prompt, invoke
297	# the agent, pipe reply through the prettifier. Shared by the four sources:
298	# cpblock (aifix/aiexplain), stdin (aifix-stdin), tee'd CMD run (aifix-run),
299	# and thefuck-style rerun (aifix-rerun).
300	#
301	#   _ai_dispatch_core <name> <source-label> <default-prompt>
302	#                     <agent> <raw> <no-meta> <prompt-override> <block>
303	_ai_dispatch_core() {
304	  local name="$1" source_label="$2" default_prompt="$3"
305	  local agent="$4" raw="$5" no_meta="$6" prompt_override="$7" block="$8"
306	  if [ -z "$block" ]; then
307	    printf '%s\n' "$name: empty block" >&2
308	    return 1
309	  fi
310	  local prompt="${prompt_override:-$default_prompt}
311	
312	$block"
313	  printf '%s\n' "$name ← $source_label" >&2
314	
315	  # Per-call env overrides: --no-meta / --raw flip env-var behaviour locally
316	  # so _aiagent_invoke + _aicap_prettify see the intended values.
317	  local saved_show="$AICAP_SHOW_METADATA" saved_pretty="$AICAP_PRETTIFY"
318	  (( no_meta )) && AICAP_SHOW_METADATA=0
319	  (( raw ))    && AICAP_PRETTIFY=0
320	
321	  if (( raw )); then
322	    _aiagent_invoke "$agent" "$prompt"
323	  else
324	    _aiagent_invoke "$agent" "$prompt" | _aicap_prettify
325	  fi
326	  local rc=$?
327	
328	  AICAP_SHOW_METADATA="$saved_show"
329	  AICAP_PRETTIFY="$saved_pretty"
330	  return $rc
331	}
332	
333	# Print the shared flag-help + env-var snapshot. Used by -h on each wrapper.
334	_ai_print_help() {
335	  local name="$1" usage="$2"
336	  printf '%s\n' "usage: $name $usage"
337	  printf '%s\n' "  -a AGENT   claude | opencode | codex | agyc | cursor-agent | http (default: auto-detect)"
338	  printf '%s\n' "  -p PROMPT  override default prompt"
339	  printf '%s\n' "  --raw      disable prettify (glow/bat), print raw agent reply"
340	  printf '%s\n' "  --no-meta  suppress the stderr metadata line"
341	  printf '%s\n' ""
342	  printf '%s\n' "env vars:"
343	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_AGENT          = ${AICAP_AGENT:-<unset = auto-detect>}"
344	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL}"
345	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL = ${AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL}"
346	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_CODEX_MODEL    = ${AICAP_CODEX_MODEL}"
347	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL   = ${AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL:-<unset>}"
348	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_HTTP_URL       = ${AICAP_HTTP_URL}"
349	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_HTTP_MODEL     = ${AICAP_HTTP_MODEL}"
350	  if [ -n "${AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY:-${OPENROUTER_API_KEY:-}}" ]; then
351	    printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY   = <set>"
352	  else
353	    printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY   = <unset>"
354	  fi
355	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_SHOW_METADATA  = ${AICAP_SHOW_METADATA}"
356	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_PRETTIFY       = ${AICAP_PRETTIFY}"
357	  printf '%s\n' "  AICAP_SPINNER        = ${AICAP_SPINNER}"
358	}
359	
360	# Shared dispatcher for aifix / aiexplain. Captures via cpblock (zsh-only).
361	_ai_capture_dispatch() {
362	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
363	  local name="$1"; shift
364	  local default_prompt="$1"; shift
365	  local n=1 agent="" prompt_override="" raw=0 no_meta=0
366	  while (( $# )); do
367	    case "$1" in
368	      -a|--agent)   agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
369	      -p|--prompt)  prompt_override="$2"; shift 2 ;;
370	      --raw)        raw=1; shift ;;
371	      --no-meta)    no_meta=1; shift ;;
372	      -h|--help)    _ai_print_help "$name" "[N] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]"
373	                    printf '%s\n' "  N          block index back (default 1 = last)"
374	                    return 0 ;;
375	      --) shift; break ;;
376	      -*) printf '%s\n' "$name: unknown flag: $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
377	      *)  n="$1"; shift ;;
378	    esac
379	  done
380	  if ! [[ "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
381	    printf '%s\n' "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n)" >&2
382	    return 1
383	  fi
384	  if [ -z "$agent" ]; then
385	    if [ -n "$AICAP_AGENT" ]; then
386	      agent="$AICAP_AGENT"
387	    else
388	      agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
389	        printf '%s\n' "$name: no coding-agent CLI found on PATH (tried: opencode, claude, codex, agyc, cursor-agent)" >&2
390	        printf '%s\n' "$name: hint — set AICAP_AGENT=http to use OpenRouter / Ollama directly" >&2
391	        return 1
392	      }
393	    fi
394	  fi
395	  if ! command -v cpblock &>/dev/null; then
396	    printf '%s\n' "$name: cpblock not defined (zsh-only; loaded from dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh)" >&2
397	    printf '%s\n' "$name: in bash, use \`aifix-stdin\` / \`aifix-run\` / \`aifix-rerun\` instead" >&2
398	    return 1
399	  fi
400	  local block
401	  block=$(cpblock "$n" 2>/dev/null) || {
402	    printf '%s\n' "$name: cpblock $n failed (run 'exec zsh' if the shell pre-dates chezmoi apply)" >&2
403	    return 1
404	  }
405	  _ai_dispatch_core "$name" "block -$n" "$default_prompt" \
406	    "$agent" "$raw" "$no_meta" "$prompt_override" "$block"
407	}
408	
409	aifix() {
410	  _ai_capture_dispatch aifix \
411	    "Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific." \
412	    "$@"
413	}
414	
415	aiexplain() {
416	  _ai_capture_dispatch aiexplain \
417	    "Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. Explain what happened in plain language. Be concise." \
418	    "$@"
419	}
420	
421	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
422	# Non-tmux Tier 1: stdin / run / rerun sources
423	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
424	# These three cover the "no tmux available" case (VSCode integrated terminal,
425	# bare Ghostty without tmux, quick SSH) by NOT relying on cpblock / OSC 133.
426	# Each composes zero magic — user explicitly picks the source.
427	#
428	# See backlog/ai-capture-non-tmux-output.md for why we don't do automatic
429	# tee redirection (Tier 2) or PTY proxy wrapping (Tier 3).
430	
431	# aifix-stdin: read whatever the caller piped in. Universal.
432	#   tail -200 /var/log/nginx/error.log | aifix-stdin
433	#   curl -sS https://weird.api/thing | aifix-stdin -p "explain this JSON"
434	#   aifix-stdin < build.log
435	aifix-stdin() {
436	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
437	  local name=aifix-stdin agent="" prompt_override="" raw=0 no_meta=0
438	  local default_prompt="Here is output captured from my terminal. Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."
439	  while (( $# )); do
440	    case "$1" in
441	      -a|--agent)   agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
442	      -p|--prompt)  prompt_override="$2"; shift 2 ;;
443	      --raw)        raw=1; shift ;;
444	      --no-meta)    no_meta=1; shift ;;
445	      -h|--help)    _ai_print_help "$name" "[-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]"
446	                    printf '%s\n' "  Reads block from stdin. No tmux / cpblock dependency."
447	                    return 0 ;;
448	      *) printf '%s\n' "$name: unexpected arg: $1 (did you mean -p?)" >&2; return 1 ;;
449	    esac
450	  done
451	  if [ -z "$agent" ]; then
452	    if [ -n "$AICAP_AGENT" ]; then
453	      agent="$AICAP_AGENT"
454	    else
455	      agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
456	        printf '%s\n' "$name: no coding-agent CLI found on PATH (set AICAP_AGENT=http for OpenRouter / Ollama)" >&2
457	        return 1
458	      }
459	    fi
460	  fi
461	  # -t 0 checks if stdin is a terminal. If it is, user likely forgot to pipe.
462	  if [ -t 0 ]; then
463	    printf '%s\n' "$name: stdin is a tty — did you forget to pipe? Example:" >&2
464	    printf '%s\n' "  some-command 2>&1 | $name" >&2
465	    return 1
466	  fi
467	  local block
468	  block=$(cat)
469	  _ai_dispatch_core "$name" "stdin" "$default_prompt" \
470	    "$agent" "$raw" "$no_meta" "$prompt_override" "$block"
471	}
472	
473	# aifix-run: run CMD, tee stdout+stderr to a log, feed "$ CMD\n<output>\n(exit code: N)"
474	# to the agent. Use `--` to separate flags from the command.
475	#   aifix-run -- cargo build --release
476	#   aifix-run -p "is this safe?" -- ansible-playbook deploy.yml
477	#
478	# isatty caveat: teeing makes CMD's stdout a pipe, so TUI apps (vim, less)
479	# render in degraded mode. Don't use this for interactive tools.
480	aifix-run() {
481	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
482	  local name=aifix-run agent="" prompt_override="" raw=0 no_meta=0
483	  local default_prompt="Here is a command I ran in my terminal and its output. Diagnose any errors and suggest a concrete fix. Be brief and specific."
484	  while (( $# )); do
485	    case "$1" in
486	      -a|--agent)   agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
487	      -p|--prompt)  prompt_override="$2"; shift 2 ;;
488	      --raw)        raw=1; shift ;;
489	      --no-meta)    no_meta=1; shift ;;
490	      -h|--help)    _ai_print_help "$name" "[-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta] -- CMD [ARG...]"
491	                    printf '%s\n' "  Runs CMD with stdout+stderr teed to a log, feeds to agent."
492	                    printf '%s\n' "  Use \`--\` to separate flags from the command."
493	                    return 0 ;;
494	      --) shift; break ;;
495	      -*) printf '%s\n' "$name: unknown flag: $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
496	      *) break ;;
497	    esac
498	  done
499	  if (( $# == 0 )); then
500	    printf '%s\n' "$name: missing command. Usage: $name [flags] -- CMD [ARG...]" >&2
501	    return 1
502	  fi
503	  if [ -z "$agent" ]; then
504	    if [ -n "$AICAP_AGENT" ]; then
505	      agent="$AICAP_AGENT"
506	    else
507	      agent=$(_aiagent_autodetect) || {
508	        printf '%s\n' "$name: no coding-agent CLI found on PATH (set AICAP_AGENT=http for OpenRouter / Ollama)" >&2
509	        return 1
510	      }
511	    fi
512	  fi
513	  local log
514	  log=$(mktemp -t aifix-run.XXXXXX) || { printf '%s\n' "$name: mktemp failed" >&2; return 1; }
515	  # Record the command line as the block's first line so the agent knows
516	  # what was run.
517	  printf '%s\n' "\$ $*" > "$log"
518	  "$@" 2>&1 | tee -a "$log"
519	  # Capture pipeline exit status. zsh uses ${pipestatus[1]} (1-indexed),
520	  # bash uses ${PIPESTATUS[0]} (0-indexed).
521	  local rc
522	  if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
523	    rc=${pipestatus[1]}
524	  else
525	    rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
526	  fi
527	  printf '\n' >> "$log"
528	  printf '%s\n' "(exit code: $rc)" >> "$log"
529	  local block
530	  block=$(<"$log")
531	  rm -f "$log"
532	  _ai_dispatch_core "$name" "run \`${1}…\` (exit $rc)" "$default_prompt" \
533	    "$agent" "$raw" "$no_meta" "$prompt_override" "$block"
534	}
535	
536	# aifix-rerun: thefuck-style. Re-executes the last command from shell history
537	# via aifix-run. Prompts for confirmation unless -y, because re-running has
538	# side effects if the command isn't idempotent.
539	aifix-rerun() {
540	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
541	  local name=aifix-rerun yes=0
542	  local -a forward
543	  forward=()
544	  while (( $# )); do
545	    case "$1" in
546	      -y|--yes) yes=1; shift ;;
547	      -h|--help) _ai_print_help "$name" "[-y] [-a AGENT] [-p PROMPT] [--raw] [--no-meta]"
548	                 printf '%s\n' "  Re-executes the last command from shell history via aifix-run."
549	                 printf '%s\n' "  Prompts for confirmation unless -y (side effects beware)."
550	                 return 0 ;;
551	      *) forward+=("$1"); shift ;;
552	    esac
553	  done
554	  # fc -ln -2 -2: skip aifix-rerun itself (which is -1), grab the one before.
555	  # `fc` works in both bash and zsh.
556	  local cmd
557	  cmd=$(fc -ln -2 -2 2>/dev/null)
558	  cmd="${cmd#	}"; cmd="${cmd# }"
559	  if [ -z "$cmd" ]; then
560	    printf '%s\n' "$name: no prior command in shell history" >&2
561	    return 1
562	  fi
563	  printf '%s\n' "$name: will re-execute:" >&2
564	  printf '%s\n' "  $cmd" >&2
565	  printf '%s\n' "⚠ side effects if the command is not idempotent (network calls, file writes, etc.)" >&2
566	  if (( ! yes )); then
567	    # zsh's `read -q "var?prompt"` reads 1 char and returns 0 only for y/Y.
568	    # bash uses `read -n 1 -p "prompt" var`; we then compare $var.
569	    local reply
570	    if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
571	      read -q "reply?Proceed? [y/N] "
572	    else
573	      read -r -n 1 -p "Proceed? [y/N] " reply
574	    fi
575	    printf '\n'
576	    if [ "$reply" != "y" ] && [ "$reply" != "Y" ]; then
577	      printf '%s\n' "$name: aborted" >&2
578	      return 130
579	    fi
580	  fi
581	  # Delegate to aifix-run via eval (preserves quoting for $cmd's shell syntax).
582	  eval "aifix-run ${forward[*]} -- $cmd"
583	}
584	
585	# aiblock — launch the Python TUI (scripts/aiblock.py) resolved via
586	# chezmoi source-path, cached per-shell. The Python side reads the same
587	# AICAP_* env vars so model defaults stay consistent.
588	#
589	# History passing: `fc -ln …` only works inside the current interactive
590	# shell — a subshell doesn't inherit the in-memory history buffer and
591	# `fc -R` only pulls whatever HISTFILE has on disk (which misses unflushed
592	# recent commands). Dump the current shell's history into a temp file and
593	# hand the path to the TUI via $AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP.
594	_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT=""
595	aiblock() {
596	  [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ] && emulate -L zsh
597	  if [ -z "$_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT" ]; then
598	    local base
599	    base=$(chezmoi source-path 2>/dev/null) || {
600	      printf '%s\n' "aiblock: could not resolve chezmoi source-path" >&2
601	      return 1
602	    }
603	    _AIBLOCK_SCRIPT="$base/scripts/aiblock.py"
604	  fi
605	  if [ ! -f "$_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT" ]; then
606	    printf '%s\n' "aiblock: $_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT not found (run 'chezmoi apply' after a git pull)" >&2
607	    return 1
608	  fi
609	  local histdump
610	  histdump=$(mktemp -t aiblock-hist.XXXXXX) || {
611	    printf '%s\n' "aiblock: mktemp failed" >&2
612	    return 1
613	  }
614	  # fc -ln -30: last 30 entries, no numbering. Trailing newline per entry.
615	  fc -ln -30 > "$histdump" 2>/dev/null
616	  AIBLOCK_HIST_DUMP="$histdump" uv run --script "$_AIBLOCK_SCRIPT" "$@"
617	  local rc=$?
618	  rm -f "$histdump"
619	  return $rc
620	}

2	// Source: dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts (managed by chezmoi)
3	//
4	// Mirrors the upstream plugin from raine/workmux:

6	//
7	// Why managed here: workmux's `wm setup` writes this file on first run, but
8	// only on machines where you remembered to run setup. Tracking it in chezmoi
9	// makes the integration auto-deploy on every fresh box.
10	//
11	// Refresh strategy: `wm` itself is install-only via ansible (see
12	// dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml) — we don't auto-bump it. When
13	// you `just upgrade-tools` and workmux ships a new plugin schema, copy the
14	// upstream file over this one:
15	//   curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/raine/workmux/main/resources/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts \
16	//     > $(chezmoi source-path ~/.config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts)
17	//
18	// Companion package.json lives next to this file (also chezmoi-managed) so
19	// OpenCode resolves @opencode-ai/plugin without us shipping node_modules.
20	//
21	// Status semantics (from `workmux set-window-status --help`):
22	//   working — agent processing                (sticky; never auto-clears)
23	//   waiting — agent needs user input          (auto-clears on window focus)
24	//   done    — agent finished                  (auto-clears on window focus)
25	// See docs/tools/workmux.md for the lifecycle / leak story.
26	
27	import type { Plugin } from '@opencode-ai/plugin';
28	
29	export const WorkmuxStatusPlugin: Plugin = async ({ $ }) => {
30	  // OpenCode can emit repeated `session.status busy` events for a single turn,
31	  // and can even emit a stale trailing `busy` after `idle` at the end. Track
32	  // per-session status so workmux only sees real transitions.
33	  const lastStatusBySession = new Map<string, string>();
34	  const acceptBusyBySession = new Map<string, boolean>();
35	
36	  async function setStatus(
37	    sessionID: string | undefined,
38	    status: string,
39	  ) {
40	    if (!sessionID) {
41	      return;
42	    }
43	
44	    const previous = lastStatusBySession.get(sessionID);
45	    // Ignore the final stale `busy` OpenCode sometimes emits after a session is
46	    // already done. The next user message re-arms `working` for the new turn.
47	    if (status === 'working' && acceptBusyBySession.get(sessionID) === false) {
48	      return;
49	    }
50	    if (previous === status) {
51	      return;
52	    }
53	
54	    lastStatusBySession.set(sessionID, status);
55	    if (status === 'done') {
56	      acceptBusyBySession.set(sessionID, false);
57	    } else {
58	      acceptBusyBySession.set(sessionID, true);
59	    }
60	
61	    await $`workmux set-window-status ${status}`.quiet();
62	  }
63	
64	  return {
65	    event: async ({ event }) => {
66	      if (event.type === 'message.updated' && event.properties.info.role === 'user') {
67	        acceptBusyBySession.set(event.properties.sessionID, true);
68	      }
69	
70	      switch (event.type) {
71	        case 'session.status':
72	          if (event.properties.status.type === 'busy') {
73	            await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'working');
74	          }
75	          if (event.properties.status.type === 'idle') {
76	            await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'done');
77	          }
78	          break;
79	        case 'permission.asked':
80	        case 'question.asked':
81	          await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'waiting');
82	          break;
83	        case 'permission.replied':
84	        case 'question.replied':
85	          await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'working');
86	          break;
87	        case 'session.idle':
88	          await setStatus(event.properties.sessionID, 'done');
89	          break;
90	      }
91	    },
92	  };
93	};
94

243	def _tmux(*args: str, timeout: float = 5.0) -> str:
244	    """Run `$TSUM_TMUX_BIN ARGS...` and return stdout. Empty string on failure

246	    global _LAST_TMUX_STDERR

```text
# Herdr CLI Commands Reference

## Session Management
- `herdr` - Launch or attach to default session
- `herdr --session <name>` - Launch/attach to named session
- `herdr session list [--json]` - List all sessions
- `herdr session attach <name>` - Attach to specific session
- `herdr session stop <name>` - Terminate a session
- `herdr session delete <name>` - Remove a session

## Workspace Commands
- `herdr workspace list` - Display all workspaces
- `herdr workspace create [--cwd PATH] [--label TEXT]` - Create new workspace
- `herdr workspace focus <id>` - Switch to workspace
- `herdr workspace close <id>` - Close workspace
- `herdr workspace rename <id> <label>` - Rename workspace

## Pane Operations
- `herdr pane list` - Show all panes
- `herdr pane current` - Get active pane
- `herdr pane focus --direction <left|right|up|down>` - Navigate between panes
- `herdr pane split [--direction right|down]` - Create new pane
- `herdr pane send-text <pane_id> <text>` - Send input to pane
- `herdr pane send-keys <pane_id> <key>` - Submit key combinations
- `herdr pane run <pane_id> <command>` - Execute command (text + Enter atomically)
- `herdr pane read <pane_id> [--source visible|recent]` - Read pane output
- `herdr pane close <pane_id>` - Close pane

## Agent Commands
- `herdr agent list` - Display all agents
- `herdr agent get <target>` - Query specific agent
- `herdr agent send <target> <text>` - Write to agent stream
- `herdr agent start <name> -- <argv>` - Launch new agent
- `herdr agent wait <target> --status <state>` - Block until state change
- `herdr agent attach <target>` - Connect to agent

## Server/Status
- `herdr status` - Check system status
- `herdr server` - Run headless server
- `herdr server reload-config` - Apply configuration changes
- `herdr server stop` - Shutdown server

## Wait Commands (Scriptable)
- `herdr wait output <pane_id> --match <text>` - Block until text appears
- `herdr wait agent-status <pane_id> --status <state>` - Block until agent state changes

These commands support JSON output for external tools like fzf or session managers to programmatically control Herdr sessions and automation workflows.
```

```text
# Herdr Configuration Overview

## Config File Location
Configuration lives at `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`. Herdr functions without a config file, applying safe defaults when values are invalid or missing.

## Custom Keybindings

Herdr supports custom command keybindings with three execution types:

- **`type = "pane"`**: Opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits
- **`type = "shell"`**: Runs detached in the background
- **`type = "plugin_action"`**: Invokes installed plugin action IDs

Example structure:
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+alt+g"
type = "pane"
command = "lazygit"
description = "run lazygit"
```

Custom commands receive environment variables including `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, and `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` when available. Shell commands execute from the focused pane's working directory.

**Limitation**: The documentation shows only built-in actions and plugin actions—arbitrary shell commands appear limited to the `type = "shell"` detached execution model.

## Keybinding Structure

No nested keytables or prefix tables exist. Instead, "keybinding strings are explicit: `prefix+n` means press the configured prefix and then `n`; `ctrl+alt+n` is a direct terminal-mode shortcut."

The `[keys]` table defines all bindings. Indexed keybindings use `1..9` notation:
```toml
[keys]
switch_tab = "prefix+1..9"
switch_workspace = "prefix+shift+1..9"
```

Navigate-mode shortcuts (workspace/pane navigation) accept plain keys like `j` or `k` but exclude `prefix+`, `esc`, `enter`, `tab`, and unmodified `1`-`9`.

## Themes

Themes are configured via:
```toml
[theme]
name = "catppuccin"
auto_switch = true
light_name = "catppuccin-latte"
dark_name = "catppuccin"
```

Built-in options include `catppuccin`, `tokyo-night`, `dracula`, `nord`, `gruvbox`, `solarized`, and others. Individual colors can be overridden:
```toml
[theme.custom]
panel_bg = "reset"
accent = "#a6e3a1"
```

## UI and Sidebar Configuration

The `[ui]` section controls dashboard appearance:
```toml
[ui]
sidebar_width = 32
sidebar_min_width = 18
sidebar_max_width = 36
mobile_width_threshold = 64
mouse_capture = true
pane_borders = true
pane_gaps = true
confirm_close = true
prompt_new_tab_name = true
```

**No status bar customization, per-pane/per-tab status text, or custom format strings are documented.** Copy-mode and vi-mode bindings are not mentioned.

## Notifications and Sound

```toml
[ui.toast]
delivery = "off"  # or "herdr", "terminal", "system"
delay_seconds = 1

[ui.toast.herdr]
position = "bottom-right"

[ui.sound]
enabled = true
path = "sounds/notification.mp3"
done_path = "sounds/done.mp3"
request_path = "sounds/request.mp3"

[ui.sound.agents]
droid = "off"
claude = "on"
```

## Terminal Defaults

```toml
[terminal]
default_shell = "nu"
shell_mode = "auto"  # or "login", "non_login"
new_cwd = "follow"   # or "home", "current", or fixed path
```

## Additional Sections

- **`[update]`**: Channel (`stable`/`preview`), version checking, manifest checking
- **`[worktrees]`**: Directory for Git worktree checkouts
- **`[remote]`**: SSH config management (`manage_ssh_config = true`)
- **`[advanced]`**: Scrollback buffer size (`scrollback_limit_bytes`)
- **`[experimental]`**: Pane history, nested launches, Kitty graphics, IME cursor tracking, input source switching

## Environment Variables

- `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH`: Override config location
- `HERDR_SESSION`: Select named session
- `HERDR_LOG`: Set log filtering (e.g., `herdr=debug`)
- `HERDR_DISABLE_SOUND`: Disable audio

**Notably absent**: Popup/menu commands, floating pane definitions, vi-mode bindings, and status bar customization are not documented as configurable features.
```

1	# Custom keybindings cable channel for television (tv)
2	# Reads the same data source as the `keys-picker` ZLE widget (Alt+/) and
3	# the `bindings` shell function: ~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md
4	#
5	# Format contract (enforced by the picker too): every row is
6	#   | `<KEY>` | `<widget>` | <description> |
7	# parsed by awk -F'|' on lines that start with `| \``.
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   tv keybindings                          (CLI)
11	#   bindings                                (shell function fallback)
12	#   Alt+/                                   (ZLE widget — the canonical entry)
13	#
14	# Keybindings inside the picker:
15	#   Enter      Paste "# <key> → <widget>: <desc>" comment
16	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy the key combo to clipboard
17	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel (live `bindkey` lookup + source grep)
18	
19	[metadata]
20	name = "keybindings"
21	description = "Zsh keybindings cheatsheet: search built-in / plugin / custom widgets"
22	
23	[source]
24	command = """
25	awk -F'|' '
26	    /^[[:space:]]*\\|[[:space:]]*`/ {
27	        key=$2; widget=$3; desc=$4
28	        for (i in arr) delete arr[i]
29	        n = split("key widget desc", arr, " ")
30	        for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
31	            v = (arr[i] == "key") ? key : (arr[i] == "widget") ? widget : desc
32	            gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, "", v)
33	            gsub(/^`|`$/, "", v)
34	            if (arr[i] == "key")    key = v
35	            if (arr[i] == "widget") widget = v
36	            if (arr[i] == "desc")   desc = v
37	        }
38	        if (key == "Key" || key ~ /^-+$/) next
39	        if (key == "<KEY>") next
40	        printf "%-16s  %-32s  %s\\n", key, widget, desc
41	    }
42	' ~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md
43	"""
44	
45	[preview]
46	command = """
47	key=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $1}')
48	widget=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $2}')
49	echo "Key:    $key"
50	echo "Widget: $widget"
51	echo
52	echo '── Live bindkey lookup (emacs keymap) ──'
53	case "$key" in
54	  Ctrl+*)
55	    ksym=$(printf '^%s' "${key#Ctrl+}")
56	    bindkey -M emacs "$ksym" 2>/dev/null || echo '(not bound)'
57	    ;;
58	  Alt+*)
59	    rest=${key#Alt+}
60	    rest=$(printf '%s' "$rest" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
61	    ksym=$(printf '\\e%s' "$rest")
62	    bindkey -M emacs "$ksym" 2>/dev/null || echo '(not bound)'
63	    ;;
64	  Tab) bindkey -M emacs '^I' 2>/dev/null ;;
65	  End) bindkey -M emacs '^[[F' 2>/dev/null ;;
66	  *)   echo '(no live lookup)' ;;
67	esac
68	echo
69	echo '── Source files in ~/.config/zsh ──'
70	if [ -d "$HOME/.config/zsh" ]; then
71	    grep -rn "^${widget}()\\|zle -N ${widget}\\b" "$HOME/.config/zsh" 2>/dev/null | head -5
72	fi
73	"""
74	
75	[keybindings]
76	enter = "actions:paste"
77	ctrl-y = "actions:copy"
78	
79	[actions.paste]
80	description = "Paste 'key → widget: desc' comment"
81	command = """
82	key=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $1}')
83	widget=$(printf '%s' '{}' | awk '{print $2}')
84	desc=$(printf '%s' '{}' | sed -E 's/^[^ ]+ +[^ ]+ +//')
85	printf '# %s → %s: %s' "$key" "$widget" "$desc"
86	"""
87	mode = "execute"

97	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then
98	    printf '%s' "$key" | xclip -selection clipboard
99	fi
100	"""
101	mode = "fork"
102

```text
1	# Live agent panes cable channel for television (tv)
2	#
3	# Discovers coding-agent sessions currently running inside any tmux pane and
4	# lets you jump straight to them. Companion to `agent-sessions.toml` (which
5	# browses STORED sessions). Backed by `agent-sessions.py panes`.
6	#
7	# Usage:
8	#   tv agent-panes
9	#   prefix + a (inside tmux)
10	#
11	# Source: 9-col TSV from `agent-sessions.py panes`:
12	#   0. agent tag       ([cc] / [cx] / [oc] / [cu])
13	#   1. when            (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM, last activity)
14	#   2. session id      (full id; empty for non-Claude when no cwd match)
15	#   3. directory       (cwd of the pane; "?" when unknown)
16	#   4. title/snippet   (Claude session name, or first non-system user msg)
17	#   5. specstory_path  (matching .specstory/history/*.md, when present)
18	#   6. pane target     (session:win.pane — passed to tmux switch-client)
19	#   7. pane pid        (tmux pane_pid; for diagnostics)
20	#   8. status glyph    (●=busy / ○=idle for Claude; empty otherwise — pre-
21	#                       rendered in Python because TV's display template
22	#                       does not support per-column substitution)
23	#
24	# Keybindings:
25	#   Enter      Switch tmux focus to that pane (session, window, pane)
26	#   Alt+T      Same as Enter (T for "take over" — mirrors agent-sessions.toml)
27	#   Alt+K      Kill the pane (confirm prompt)
28	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy pane target (session:win.pane) to clipboard
29	#   Alt+P      Copy directory path to clipboard
30	#   Alt+R      Copy session id to clipboard
31	#   Alt+S      Copy matched .specstory/history/*.md path to clipboard
32	#
33	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
34	#   1. Live tmux capture-pane snapshot (last ~80 lines of the pane).
35	#   2. Stored transcript (delegates to agent-sessions.py transcript mode).
36	
37	[metadata]
38	name = "agent-panes"
39	description = "Live coding-agent panes across tmux — jump to a running claude/codex/opencode/cursor session"
40	requirements = ["tmux", "python3"]
41	
42	[source]
43	command = "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py panes"
44	# Display: agent + status glyph + pane target │ snippet │ short cwd
45	# Glyph (col 8) is pre-rendered in Python — see comment in agent-sessions.py
46	# `_build_pane_row`. TV silently breaks ALL `{split:}` substitutions in the
47	# same string when it sees unrecognised syntax (e.g. `s/busy/●/`).
48	display = "{split:\t:0} {split:\t:8} {split:\t:6}  │  {split:\t:4}  │  {split:\t:3|split:/:-1}"
49	output = "{split:\t:6}"
50	
51	[preview]
52	command = [
53	  # Preview 1 (default): live capture-pane snapshot.
54	  # Shows what's actually on screen in that pane RIGHT NOW — the most useful
55	  # thing when you're about to jump to it.
56	  '''
57	  target='{split:\t:6}'; agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; pane_status='{split:\t:8}'; pid='{split:\t:7}'
58	  # NB: `status` is read-only in zsh ($? alias) — DO NOT rename `pane_status` back to `status`.
59	  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  pane=%s  pid=%s  %s\n' "$agent" "$target" "$pid" "$pane_status"
60	  printf '\033[2msession:\033[0m  %s\n' "$sid"
61	  printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m      %s\n' '{split:\t:3}'
62	  printf '\n\033[1m─── live pane (capture-pane -ep) ───\033[0m\n'
63	  tmux capture-pane -ep -t "$target" 2>/dev/null | tail -n 80 \
64	    || echo "(pane $target no longer exists — picker is stale; press Ctrl+R to reload)"
65	  ''',
66	  # Preview 2: stored transcript (markdown-rendered).
67	  # `glow --style auto` degrades to plain when stdout is a pipe (which is
68	  # always true in TV's preview pane); force `--style dark` to keep ANSI.
69	  # Width is taken from $TV_PREVIEW_WIDTH if TV exports it, else COLUMNS.
70	  '''
71	  agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'
72	  case "$agent" in
73	    "[cc]") tag=cc ;;
74	    "[cx]") tag=cx ;;
75	    "[oc]") tag=oc ;;
76	    *) tag="" ;;
77	  esac
78	  if [ -z "$tag" ] || [ -z "$sid" ]; then
79	    printf '\033[2m(no stored transcript for %s — use preview 1 for live pane content.)\033[0m\n' "$agent"
80	    exit 0
81	  fi
82	  W="${TV_PREVIEW_WIDTH:-${COLUMNS:-100}}"
83	  if command -v glow >/dev/null 2>&1; then
84	    "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null \
85	      | glow --style dark -w "$W" - 2>/dev/null \
86	      || "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null \
87	        | bat -l md --color=always --paging=never --style=plain 2>/dev/null \
88	      || "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null
89	  else
90	    "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null \
91	      | bat -l md --color=always --paging=never --style=plain 2>/dev/null \
92	      || "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null
93	  fi
94	  ''',
95	]
96	header = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:6}  ({split:\t:3|split:/:-1})"
97	
98	[ui]
99	input_header = "Live Agent Panes"
100	
101	[ui.preview_panel]
102	size = 60
103	
104	[keybindings]
105	enter = "actions:switch_pane"
106	alt-t = "actions:switch_pane"
107	alt-k = "actions:kill_pane"
108	ctrl-y = "actions:copy_target"
109	alt-p = "actions:copy_dir"
110	alt-r = "actions:copy_id"
111	alt-s = "actions:copy_specstory"
112	
113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	# Actions — keep shell glue minimal; any bare `{` would silently break TV's
115	# own placeholder substitution. See agent-sessions.toml line ~80.
116	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
117	
118	[actions.switch_pane]
119	description = "Switch tmux focus to that session/window/pane"
120	command = '''
121	target='{split:\t:6}'
122	[ -z "$target" ] && exit 0
123	session="${target%%:*}"
124	winpane="${target#*:}"
125	window="${winpane%.*}"
126	pane="${winpane#*.}"
127	# switch-client moves the attached client to the target session; select-window
128	# and select-pane scope down. We run as three steps so a missing pane (stale
129	# row) doesn't leave focus mid-jump.
130	tmux switch-client -t "$session" 2>/dev/null \
131	  && tmux select-window -t "$session:$window" 2>/dev/null \
132	  && tmux select-pane -t "$target" 2>/dev/null \
133	  || tmux display-message "agent-panes: pane $target no longer exists (stale row)"
134	'''
135	mode = "fork"
136	
137	[actions.kill_pane]
138	description = "Kill the pane (confirm prompt)"
139	command = '''
140	target='{split:\t:6}'
141	[ -z "$target" ] && exit 0
142	printf 'Kill pane %s? [y/N] ' "$target"
143	read -r ans
144	case "$ans" in
145	  y|Y|yes|YES)
146	    tmux kill-pane -t "$target" 2>/dev/null \
147	      && echo "killed $target" \
148	      || echo "failed to kill $target (already gone?)"
149	    ;;
150	  *) echo "aborted" ;;
151	esac
152	echo "[Press Enter]"; read -r _
153	'''
154	mode = "execute"
155	
156	[actions.copy_target]
157	description = "Copy pane target (session:win.pane) to clipboard"
158	command = '''
159	d='{split:\t:6}'
160	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
161	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
162	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
163	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
164	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
165	fi
166	'''
167	mode = "fork"
168	
169	[actions.copy_id]
170	description = "Copy session ID to clipboard"
171	command = '''
172	d='{split:\t:2}'
173	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
174	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
175	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
176	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
177	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
178	fi
179	'''
180	mode = "fork"
181	
182	[actions.copy_dir]
183	description = "Copy directory path to clipboard"
184	command = '''
185	d='{split:\t:3}'
186	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
187	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
188	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
189	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
190	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
191	fi
192	'''
193	mode = "fork"
194	
195	[actions.copy_specstory]
196	description = "Copy .specstory/history/*.md path to clipboard"
197	command = '''
198	d='{split:\t:5}'
199	[ -z "$d" ] && exit 0
200	if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy
201	elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy
202	elif command -v xclip >/dev/null 2>&1; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard
203	else printf '\033]52;c;%s\007' "$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" > /dev/tty
204	fi

1	# 37_worktrunk.sh - Worktrunk (`wt`) shell integration (shared bash + zsh).
2	# https://worktrunk.dev — github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk
3	#
4	# Backend half of the split: shell-init wrapper (so `wt switch` can change
5	# the parent shell's $PWD) + the `wtcd` fzf picker. Zsh-only half lives in
6	# dot_config/zsh/tools/37_worktrunk.zsh (clap-based completion generation
7	# into ~/.zfunc/_wt).
8	#
9	# Companion config: ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml (managed by chezmoi at
10	# dot_config/worktrunk/config.toml). Aliases like `wt sw` / `wt cc` live
11	# THERE, not here — keep this file focused on shell-level integration only.
12	
13	# Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline)
14	command -v wt &>/dev/null || return 0
15	
16	# ── Shell integration: cd-wrapping `wt` function ───────────────────────────
17	#
18	# `wt switch` needs to change the parent shell's $PWD, which a normal binary
19	# can't do. Worktrunk solves this by writing a directive file that a wrapper
20	# shell function reads and `cd`s to. We eval that wrapper at shell startup
21	# rather than running `wt config shell install` (which edits ~/.zshrc with a
22	# block chezmoi would fight over).
23	#
24	# Same pattern as starship / zoxide / direnv elsewhere. The `2>/dev/null`
25	# swallows the error if wt doesn't support the requested shell (e.g. bash
26	# wrapper not yet implemented in upstream) — the binary itself still works,
27	# users just lose the cd-on-switch wrapper.
28	if [ -n "$ZSH_VERSION" ]; then
29	    eval "$(wt config shell init zsh 2>/dev/null)"
30	elif [ -n "$BASH_VERSION" ]; then
31	    eval "$(wt config shell init bash 2>/dev/null)"
32	fi
33	
34	# ── Tiny shell-side conveniences (NOT duplicating wt's own aliases) ────────
35	#
36	# `wt`'s own aliases (sw / ls / rm / cc / oc) are defined in
37	# ~/.config/worktrunk/config.toml so they work from any shell + the
38	# interactive picker. Anything below is shell niceness that wt's alias
39	# system can't express.
40	
41	# `wtcd` — jump to a worktree path WITHOUT switching tmux/sesh session.
42	# Useful when you want to peek at sibling worktree files (open in nvim split,
43	# scp, etc.) without disturbing the current pane's session context.
44	function wtcd() {
45	    local target
46	    target=$(wt list --format=json 2>/dev/null \
47	        | jq -r '.worktrees[].path' \
48	        | fzf-tmux -p 60%,40% --prompt='wt cd ❯ ' --header='Pick a worktree to cd into') \
49	        || return
50	    [ -n "$target" ] && cd -- "$target"
51	}
52
```

1	# 38_workmux.sh - Workmux (`workmux` / `wm`) tmux + git-worktree orchestrator
2	# (shared bash + zsh). Moved from dot_config/zsh/tools/38_workmux.zsh; the
3	# only zsh-ism was `${(@f)$(cmd)}` (split-on-newlines flag), rewritten as a
4	# `while IFS= read -r` loop.
5	#
6	# https://workmux.raine.dev — github.com/raine/workmux
7	#
8	# Companion config: ~/.config/workmux/config.yaml (managed by chezmoi at
9	# dot_config/workmux/config.yaml). See docs/tools/workmux.md for the full
10	# story (worktrunk vs workmux split, status icon lifecycle, leak mitigation).
11	#
12	# Why a separate file from 37_worktrunk.{sh,zsh}: the two tools coexist
13	# (worktrunk = `wt` for git-worktree CLI / aliases, workmux = `wm` for status
14	# icons + dashboard + sidebar). Separate files keep the rationale + helpers
15	# per-tool and let users disable one independently.
16	
17	# Skip silently if not installed (Linux ansible install can fail offline,
18	# Cargo path may not be present, etc.)
19	command -v workmux &>/dev/null || return 0
20	
21	# ── Manual marker cleanup ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
22	#
23	# The `working` (🤖) status workmux sets is *sticky* — it never auto-clears
24	# on its own. `waiting` (💬) and `done` (✅) auto-clear when you focus the
25	# window, but `working` only goes away when:
26	#   1. The agent's plugin/hook explicitly calls `workmux set-window-status done`
27	#      (Claude Stop / OpenCode session.idle), OR
28	#   2. `workmux sidebar` is running and detects 10s of pane silence
29	#      (interrupted-agent detection), OR
30	#   3. You manually clear it.
31	#
32	# Path #1 fails when the agent is killed before its Stop/idle handler fires
33	# (Ctrl+C, terminal crash, OOM). Path #2 requires keeping a sidebar pane open.
34	# `wmclear` is the manual escape hatch.
35	#
36	# Without arg: clears the marker for the current tmux window.
37	# With arg:    `wmclear 5` clears window 5 in the current session.
38	# Pass `--all` to nuke every workmux marker in the current session.
39	function wmclear() {
40	    if [[ "$1" == "--all" ]]; then
41	        # Walk every window in the current session and unset the user-var.
42	        # Original zsh code used `windows=("${(@f)$(...)}")` to split command
43	        # output on newlines; the `while IFS= read -r` loop below is the
44	        # portable equivalent (works in bash + zsh).
45	        local sess
46	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
47	        local -a windows
48	        windows=()
49	        local w
50	        while IFS= read -r w; do
51	            [ -n "$w" ] && windows+=( "$w" )
52	        done < <(tmux list-windows -t "$sess" -F '#{window_index}' 2>/dev/null)
53	        for w in "${windows[@]}"; do
54	            tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${w}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
55	        done
56	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${#windows[@]} windows in session $sess"
57	        return 0
58	    fi
59	
60	    if [[ -n "$1" ]]; then
61	        # Specific window: use workmux's own clear command (handles agent
62	        # state too, not just the tmux user-var)
63	        local sess win
64	        sess=$(tmux display -p '#{session_name}' 2>/dev/null) || return 1
65	        win="$1"
66	        tmux set-option -w -t "${sess}:${win}" -u '@workmux_status' 2>/dev/null
67	        echo "Cleared @workmux_status on ${sess}:${win}"
68	        return 0
69	    fi
70	
71	    # Current window: prefer workmux's clear so it also resets agent state
72	    workmux set-window-status clear 2>/dev/null
73	}
74	
75	# ── Sidebar daemon convenience ─────────────────────────────────────────────
76	#
77	# `workmux sidebar` is what enables the "interrupted agent" auto-clear (10s
78	# pane-silence heuristic). Without it, `working` markers leak forever on
79	# crashed agents. NOT auto-started here because it spawns a tmux pane and
80	# many users want to opt-in. Use `wmsb` to toggle.
81	alias wmsb='workmux sidebar'
82	
83	# ── Short aliases mirroring upstream's recommendation ──────────────────────
84	# README explicitly suggests `alias wm='workmux'`. The Linux ansible install
85	# also creates a `wm` symlink in ~/.local/bin so this alias is redundant on
86	# Linux, but on macOS Homebrew installs only `workmux`, so define it here.
87	if ! command -v wm &>/dev/null; then
88	    alias wm='workmux'
89	fi
90
```
</details></tool-use>

1	# 37_worktrunk.zsh - Worktrunk (`wt`) zsh-only completion generation.
2	# Shell-init wrapper + wtcd function live in dot_config/shell/37_worktrunk.sh

10	# ── Completion ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
11	#
12	# macOS (Homebrew): `_wt` ships in /opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/
13	# and is picked up automatically by compinit — nothing to do here.
14	#
15	# Linux (ansible drops the bare binary into ~/.local/bin/) has no system
16	# completion path, so dump clap's auto-generated zsh completer into
17	# ~/.zfunc/_wt (already on $fpath via dot_zshrc.tmpl). Same pattern as sesh /
18	# television. Regenerate when wt's version changes.
19	#
20	# Worktrunk doesn't expose a `wt completion zsh` subcommand — clap's dynamic
21	# completer is invoked via `COMPLETE=zsh wt` (with no args). Output is a
22	# self-contained `#compdef wt` script that handles further completion
23	# requests by re-invoking the binary with COMPLETE+_CLAP_COMPLETE_INDEX set.
24	if [[ -d ~/.zfunc ]] && [[ ! -f /opt/homebrew/share/zsh/site-functions/_wt ]] \
25	                    && [[ ! -f /usr/local/share/zsh/site-functions/_wt ]]; then
26	    local _wt_ver="$(wt --version 2>/dev/null)"
27	    if [[ ! -f ~/.zfunc/_wt ]] || ! grep -q "${_wt_ver}" ~/.zfunc/_wt 2>/dev/null; then
28	        {
29	            print -r -- "# Auto-generated by 37_worktrunk.zsh for ${_wt_ver}"
30	            COMPLETE=zsh wt 2>/dev/null
31	        } > ~/.zfunc/_wt
32	    fi
33	fi
34

2	#
3	# Unified browser for OpenCode + Claude Code + Codex + Cursor sessions.
4	# Backed by `dot_config/television/executable_agent-sessions.py` (Python helper

6	#
7	# Usage:

9	#
10	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
11	#   1. All agents merged       (default — globally sorted DESC by mtime)
12	#   2. OpenCode only           (~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db)
13	#   3. Claude Code only        (~/.claude/projects/**/<sid>.jsonl)
14	#   4. Codex only              (~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl)
15	#   5. Cursor Agent CLI only   (~/.cursor/chats/<wsHash>/<chatId>/store.db)
16	#   6. Cursor IDE composers    (~/Library/Application Support/Cursor/User/{globalStorage,workspaceStorage})
17	#
18	# Agent tags: [oc] OpenCode, [cc] Claude Code, [cx] Codex,
19	#             [cu] Cursor Agent CLI, [ci] Cursor IDE composer chats
20	#
21	# Title/snippet column is the first non-system user message (truncated 140ch),
22	# so TV's fuzzy search matches by content as well as date / project / id.
23	#
24	# Each row also carries a matched `.specstory/history/*.md` path (col 5) when
25	# SpecStory has written one for that session — see docs/tools/specstory-internals.md.
26	#
27	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
28	#   1. Metadata header + full chat transcript (glow-rendered; prefers the
29	#      .specstory/history/*.md file when present, falls back to raw-source
30	#      walk for live sessions). Cursor [cu]/[ci] show a "deferred" note and
31	#      the legacy first-5 view in cycle 2 instead — see the backlog entry
32	#      backlog/tv-agent-sessions-richer-preview.md.
33	#   2. Metadata header + first 5 user messages (legacy; kept for fast
34	#      content search across sessions).
35	#   3. Raw record dump (head 200 lines / SQL dump).
36	#
37	# Keybindings:
38	#   Enter      Print resume one-liner to stdout (cd <dir> && <agent-cmd> <id>)
39	#   Alt+T      Resume in same shell (cd + exec; T for "take over")
40	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy session ID to clipboard
41	#   Alt+P      Copy directory path to clipboard
42	#   Alt+R      Copy resume one-liner to clipboard
43	#   Alt+S      Copy matched .specstory/history/*.md path to clipboard (S for SpecStory)
44	#   Alt+E      Open raw session file in $EDITOR (claude/codex only)
45	#
46	# Ctrl+E is left as TV's global `go_to_input_end`.
47	
48	[metadata]
49	name = "agent-sessions"
50	description = "Coding-agent sessions: OpenCode + Claude Code + Codex + Cursor (CLI & IDE) — content-searchable"
51	requirements = ["python3", "bat"]
52	
53	[source]
54	# Each cycle calls the helper with a different mode. Mode "all" is the default.
55	# TSV columns produced by the helper:
56	#   0. agent  ([oc]/[cc]/[cx]/[cu])
57	#   1. when   (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM)
58	#   2. id     (session id)
59	#   3. dir    (cwd)
60	#   4. title/snippet

62	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py all",
63	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py opencode",
64	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py claude",
65	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py codex",
66	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py cursor",
67	  "~/.config/television/agent-sessions.py cursor-ide",
68	]
69	display = "{split:\t:0} {split:\t:1}  │  {split:\t:4}  │  {split:\t:3|split:/:-1}"
70	output = "{split:\t:2}"
71	
72	[preview]
73	command = [
74	  # Preview 1 (default): metadata header + full chat transcript.
75	  #
76	  # The transcript is rendered by the Python helper's `transcript` mode,
77	  # which prefers the matched .specstory/history/*.md file (col 5) when
78	  # present and falls back to walking the raw session source for live
79	  # sessions. Output is piped through `glow` (if installed) or `bat`.
80	  #
81	  # IMPORTANT: do NOT embed Python/awk/JSON literals inline here — any bare
82	  # `{...}` in this string (outside TV's own `{split:...}`/`{strip_ansi}`
83	  # placeholders) silently breaks ALL placeholder substitution in the same
84	  # command. See pitfalls/tv-channel-bare-braces-break-substitution.md.
85	  # Keep the rich logic in the helper; this block is just shell glue.
86	  '''
87	  agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'; when='{split:\t:1}'; ss='{split:\t:5}'
88	  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$sid" "$when"

90	  if [ -n "$ss" ]; then
91	    printf '\033[2mspecstory:\033[0m %s\n' "$ss"
92	  fi
93	  case "$agent" in
94	    "[oc]")

96	        "SELECT 'title=    ' || title || char(10) || 'version=  ' || version FROM session WHERE id = '$sid';" 2>/dev/null
97	      ;;
98	    "[cc]")

105	      ;;
106	  esac
107	  printf '\n'
108	  case "$agent" in
109	    "[cc]") tag=cc ;;
110	    "[cx]") tag=cx ;;
111	    "[oc]") tag=oc ;;
112	    *) tag="" ;;
113	  esac
114	  if [ -z "$tag" ]; then

116	    exit 0
117	  fi
118	  if command -v glow >/dev/null 2>&1; then
119	    "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null \
120	      | glow --style auto - 2>/dev/null \
121	      || "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null
122	  else
123	    "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null \
124	      | bat -l md --color=always --plain --paging=never 2>/dev/null \
125	      || "$HOME/.config/television/agent-sessions.py" transcript "$tag" "$sid" 2>/dev/null
126	  fi
127	  ''',
128	  # Preview 2 (legacy): metadata + first 5 user messages — kept because
129	  # content-searching sessions by "did I talk about X?" is faster here
130	  # than scrolling a full transcript.
131	  '''
132	  agent='{split:\t:0}'; sid='{split:\t:2}'; dir='{split:\t:3}'; when='{split:\t:1}'
133	  printf '\033[1m%s\033[0m  %s\n' "$sid" "$when"
134	  printf '\033[2mcwd:\033[0m %s\n\n' "$dir"
135	  case "$agent" in
136	    "[oc]")
137	      sqlite3 "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db" \
138	        "SELECT 'title=' || title || char(10) || 'version=' || version || char(10) || 'project_id=' || project_id || char(10) || coalesce('share=' || share_url, '') FROM session WHERE id = '$sid';" 2>/dev/null
139	      printf '\n\033[1mFirst 5 user messages:\033[0m\n'

141	        SELECT '  ' || substr(replace(replace(json_extract(p.data, '\$.text'), char(10), ' '), '  ', ' '), 1, 280)
142	        FROM part p JOIN message m ON p.message_id = m.id
143	        WHERE p.session_id = '$sid'

146	          AND p.data NOT LIKE '%\"synthetic\":true%'
147	        ORDER BY p.time_created ASC
148	        LIMIT 5;" 2>/dev/null
149	      ;;
150	    "[cc]")

2	#
3	# Shows live coding-agent panes, conservatively detected quota/rate-limit wait
4	# states, parsed reset times, and queued pueue wakeup tasks.
5	#
6	# Keybindings:

9	#   Alt+T      Prompt for custom time/delay
10	#   Alt+N      Smart send now (Enter for rate-limit menus, otherwise continue)
11	#   Alt+X      Cancel queued wakeup task(s)
12	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview (live pane capture via agent-wakeup.py)
13	
14	[metadata]
15	name = "agent-wakeup"
16	description = "Agent quota wakeup dashboard: quota waits, reset timers, scheduled continue tasks"
17	requirements = ["tmux", "python3", "pueue"]
18	
19	[source]
20	command = "~/.config/television/agent-wakeup.py status --tsv"
21	display = "{split:\t:0} {split:\t:1} {split:\t:2}  │ action {split:\t:12} │ reset {split:\t:4} │ wake {split:\t:6} │ {split:\t:8}"
22	output = "{split:\t:2}"
23	watch = 5.0
24	no_sort = true
25	
26	[preview]
27	command = "~/.config/television/agent-wakeup.py preview --pane '{split:\t:3}' || true"
28	header = "{split:\t:0}  {split:\t:1}  {split:\t:2}"
29

31	input_header = "Agent Wakeup"
32	
33	[ui.preview_panel]
34	size = 60
35	
36	[keybindings]
37	enter = "actions:switch_pane"
38	alt-c = ["actions:schedule_detected", "reload_source"]
39	alt-t = ["actions:schedule_custom", "reload_source"]
40	alt-n = ["actions:send_now", "reload_source"]
41	alt-x = ["actions:cancel", "reload_source"]
42	
43	[actions.switch_pane]
44	description = "Switch tmux focus to that pane"
45	command = '''
46	target='{split:\t:2}'
47	[ -z "$target" ] && exit 0
48	case "$target" in
49	  %*) tmux select-pane -t "$target" 2>/dev/null || tmux display-message "agent-wakeup: pane $target no longer exists" ;;
50	  *)
51	    session="${target%%:*}"

54	    tmux switch-client -t "$session" 2>/dev/null \
55	      && tmux select-window -t "$session:$window" 2>/dev/null \
56	      && tmux select-pane -t "$target" 2>/dev/null \
57	      || tmux display-message "agent-wakeup: pane $target no longer exists"
58	    ;;
59	esac
