```text
1	# Vim mode in this dotfiles repo
2	
3	Catalog of every place vim-style modal editing or vim-flavored navigation
4	is wired into this dotfiles repo, gated by a single chezmoi prompt
5	`enableVimMode` (default `true`).
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	
9	- Default: **`enableVimMode = true`** — zsh / bash / tmux all behave the
10	  same as before this flag was introduced.
11	- Set `false` (e.g. for non-vim friends, CI, the `minimal` Docker bundle)
12	  → modal editing in shells off, vim-tmux-navigator off, copy-mode goes
13	  emacs.
14	- **Neovim is never affected**, regardless of the flag. Neovim is
15	  inherently vim and stays so.
16	- **Editor configs (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI)
17	  are never affected** — this repo doesn't manage their vim-mode
18	  extensions.
19	- Re-prompt: `chezmoi init --force` (re-asks every prompt) or
20	  `chezmoi execute-template '{{ promptBoolOnce . "enableVimMode" "..." true }}'`
21	  for one-off testing. The full prompt text is in
22	  [`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl).
23	
24	## Scope: what's gated, what's not
25	
26	| Surface | `enableVimMode = true` (default) | `enableVimMode = false` |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| zsh OMZ plugins | includes `zsh-vi-mode` | omits `zsh-vi-mode` |
29	| `~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-vi-mode` git clone | cloned (chezmoi external) | not cloned |
30	| zsh `zvm_after_init` rebind block | defined | omitted (no plugin to wipe keymaps → unnecessary) |
31	| bash `set -o vi` (`05_vi_mode.bash`) | runs | replaced with no-op `:` |
32	| ble.sh `ble-bind` keymap (`04_blesh.bash`) | `-m vi_imap` / `-m vi_nmap` | default keymap (emacs) |
33	| tmux `mode-keys` (`common.conf`) | `vi` | `emacs` |
34	| tmux copy-mode bindings (`keybindings.conf`) | bound on `copy-mode-vi` table | bound on `copy-mode` table (same actions) |
35	| tmux vim-tmux-navigator (`Ctrl+h/j/k/l` root) | bound | unbound (frees `Ctrl+L` clear, `Ctrl+H` backspace, etc. for inner apps) |
36	| tmux `prefix + h/j/k/l` pane select | bound | **bound** (kept — prefix-gated, no conflict; vim-letter shortcut is harmless for non-vim users) |
37	| tmux `prefix + H/J/K/L` resize 5 cells | bound | **bound** (kept) |
38	| tmux `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` fine resize | bound | **bound** (kept) |
39	| marimo `[keymap] preset` (`create_marimo.toml`) | `vim` | `default` (FRESH installs only — `create_` prefix means the file is seeded once and never re-touched) |
40	| btop `vim_keys` (`create_btop.conf`) | `True` | `False` (FRESH installs only — `create_` prefix means the file is seeded once and never re-touched) |
41	| superfile `hotkeys.toml` (`dot_config/superfile/`) | yazi-parity vim preset (`j`/`k` nav, `y`/`x`/`p`/`d` file ops, `h` parent, `l`/Enter open, `q` quit, `a` create, `r` rename, `v` panel mode, `?` help) — adapted from upstream `vimHotkeys.toml` with `q`/`esc` quit, `h`/`←`/`backspace` parent, `right`/`l` confirm, `v` panel-mode kept | upstream default preset (`ctrl+c`/`ctrl+x`/`ctrl+v` file ops, single-letter focus keys `m`/`p`/`s`) |
42	| VisiData `~/.visidatarc` (`dot_visidatarc.tmpl`) | INSERT mnemonic: `i` → `edit-cell` (additive — `e` still works); column nav: `0` / `$` / `_` / `^` → `go-leftmost` / `go-rightmost` (mirrors vim line-internal chars); displaced commands relocated to `z$` (type-currency), `zw` (resize-col-max), `zN` (rename-col) | no rebind — `i` stays bound to `addcol-incr`; `$` / `_` / `^` keep their VisiData defaults (`type-currency`, `resize-col-max`, `rename-col`); `gh`/`gl` remain the canonical column-jump keystrokes |
43	| Neovim (`dot_config/nvim/`) | unchanged | **unchanged** (out of scope by design) |
44	| VSCode / Cursor / Antigravity vim extension | not managed | **not managed** (out of scope) |
45	| Codex / OpenCode / Cursor-CLI vim mode | not managed | **not managed** (out of scope) |
46	
47	## The gate: `enableVimMode` chezmoi prompt
48	
49	Defined in [`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoi.toml.tmpl)
50	near the `primaryShell` line. The exact prompt text is reproduced below
51	because **`chezmoi init --promptBool` matches by full prompt text, not
52	by key**, so it must be byte-identical across `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`,
53	`Dockerfile`, and `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py PROMPTS`:
54	
55	```
56	Enable vim-style modal editing in shells (zsh-vi-mode, set -o vi,
57	ble.sh vi-mode) and tmux vim navigation (vim-tmux-navigator
58	C-h/j/k/l, mode-keys vi); does NOT affect Neovim
59	```
60	
61	The "does NOT affect Neovim" tail is deliberate — it's there so the
62	prompt itself reassures vim-fluent users who'd otherwise hesitate to
63	opt out for fear of losing their editor.
64	
65	**Three-file rule**: any new chezmoi prompt must be added to
66	`.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `Dockerfile` ARG + `dotfiles_init.py PROMPTS`
67	in the same commit. `enableVimMode` follows that rule. Verify with:
68	
69	```bash
70	uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor
71	```
72	
73	(Note: pre-existing `installTunnelTools` drift in the script/Dockerfile
74	is unrelated to this prompt and tracked separately.)
75	
76	**Bundle behavior** (`scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py BUNDLES`):
77	
78	- `personal-mac`, `work-mac`, `server-linux`, `custom` — fall through
79	  to default `True` (vim mode on).
80	- `minimal` — explicitly forces `enableVimMode = False` because CI /
81	  Docker doesn't benefit from modal editing and emacs-keymap shells
82	  match what most automation expects.
83	
84	## Catalog: every vim touch-point in the repo
85	
86	### Shell layer
87	
88	#### zsh — `zsh-vi-mode` plugin
89	
90	**File**: [`dot_zshrc.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_zshrc.tmpl)
91	lines ~21–53.
92	
93	The plugin (`jeffreytse/zsh-vi-mode`) is added to OMZ's plugin array,
94	and a `zvm_after_init` hook re-applies fzf / atuin (`Alt+R`) /
95	aisuggest (`Alt+;`) / keys-picker (`Alt+/`) bindings across `viins`,
96	`vicmd`, and `emacs` keymaps. The hook exists because zsh-vi-mode
97	**wipes all keymaps on init** — without re-binding, `Ctrl+R` would
98	stop launching atuin etc.
99	
100	When `enableVimMode = false`, both the plugin entry and the
101	`zvm_after_init` block are gated out. The picker tools
102	(`dot_config/zsh/tools/{05_aisuggest,11_tools_picker,12_television,13_keys_picker,22_sesh}.zsh`)
103	each call `bindkey -M emacs` at source-time, so without the wiping
104	plugin those bindings stick on first source — no rebind hook needed.
105	
106	**External clone**: [`.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl)
107	lines ~55–62 — the `git-repo` entry that clones the plugin into
108	`~/.oh-my-zsh/custom/plugins/zsh-vi-mode` is also gated, saving a
109	network round-trip on opt-out hosts.
110	
111	**Harmless leftovers** (intentionally not gated): the `bindkey -M viins`
112	/ `bindkey -M vicmd` lines inside the picker tool files are no-ops when
113	zsh-vi-mode isn't loaded — keeping them avoids cluttering each tool
114	file with another conditional.
115	
116	#### bash — `set -o vi` + ble.sh vi keymap
117	
118	**Files**:
119	[`dot_config/bash/05_vi_mode.bash.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/bash/05_vi_mode.bash.tmpl) (single `set -o vi` line),
120	[`dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/bash/04_blesh.bash.tmpl) (vi-mode-aware ble.sh tweaks).
121	
122	`set -o vi` is **the trigger** for ble.sh's vi-mode (ble.sh auto-detects
123	readline vi mode at attach time). When opted out:
124	
125	- `05_vi_mode.bash.tmpl` body becomes `:` (no-op) → readline stays in
126	  default emacs keymap, ble.sh stays in default keymap.
127	- `04_blesh.bash.tmpl` swaps the four `ble-bind -m vi_imap`/`vi_nmap`
128	  calls (`C-RET` / `S-RET` accept-line, `C-c` discard-line) to plain
129	  `ble-bind` (binds in current/emacs keymap), so multi-line submit and
130	  Ctrl+C cancel still work the way zsh users expect.
131	
132	**Why both files were renamed to `.tmpl`**: `dot_config/bash/` is
133	otherwise a non-templated drop-in directory loaded by
134	`load_modular_dir` from `dot_bashrc.tmpl`. Adding `.tmpl` to specific
135	files lets chezmoi process the `{{ if .enableVimMode }}` blocks while
136	the rest of the `*.bash` files in the dir stay verbatim. chezmoi
137	deploys the templated file at `~/.config/bash/04_blesh.bash` (suffix
138	stripped) — same target path, same load order.
139	
140	**Out of scope**: oh-my-bash plugins are loaded by name from `OSH_PLUGINS`
141	in [`dot_bashrc.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_bashrc.tmpl);
142	none of the loaded plugins are vim-mode-related (the `vi-mode` OMB
143	plugin is intentionally *not* loaded — ble.sh's vi-mode is much
144	better when it's on, and `set -o vi` is enough when ble.sh isn't).
145	
146	### Multiplexer layer
147	
148	#### tmux — `mode-keys vi` + `copy-mode-vi` table
149	
150	**Files**:
151	[`dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl) (line ~68: `mode-keys`),
152	[`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl)
153	(lines ~98–120: `copy-mode-vi` table bindings).
154	
155	Both files renamed to `.tmpl` — same target path on apply.
156	
157	`mode-keys` selects the table tmux's copy-mode dispatches keys against:
158	
159	- `vi` table (`copy-mode-vi`): `h/j/k/l` cursor, `v` begin-selection,
160	  `V` line-select, `C-v` rectangle-toggle, `y` copy-and-cancel,
161	  `gg` / `G` top/bottom, `/` / `?` search.
162	- `emacs` table (`copy-mode`): `Ctrl+B`/`Ctrl+F`/`Ctrl+N`/`Ctrl+P`
163	  cursor, `Space` begin-selection, `Meta+w` copy.
164	
165	Custom bindings in this repo (`v`, `V`, `C-v`, `y`,
166	`MouseDragEnd1Pane`, `DoubleClick1Pane`, `{` / `}` previous/next
167	prompt, `M-[` / `M-]` previous/next output) are templated to bind
168	under the **active table** based on `enableVimMode`:
169	
170	```
171	{{- $copyTable := "copy-mode" -}}
172	{{- if .enableVimMode -}}{{ $copyTable = "copy-mode-vi" }}{{- end }}
173	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} v send-keys -X begin-selection
174	...
175	```
176	
177	The `send-keys -X begin-selection` action itself is table-agnostic, so
178	the same five lines work for both tables. The `prefix + M-y` / `M-i`
179	macros at lines ~147–165 (Warp-style copy-last-output / copy-last-input)
180	are **not** templated — they use `send-keys -X previous-prompt` /
181	`next-prompt` which work regardless of `mode-keys`.
182	
183	#### tmux — vim-tmux-navigator (root-table `Ctrl+h/j/k/l`)
184	
185	**File**: [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl) lines ~181–192.
186	
187	Implements the [christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator](https://github.com/christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator)
188	contract via `bind-key -n` (root-table, no prefix) on `Ctrl+h/j/k/l`:
189	`is_vim` heuristic forwards the key to the inner pane if it's running
190	vim/nvim, otherwise calls `select-pane -L/-D/-U/-R`. Plus 4 mirrors on
191	the `copy-mode-vi` table so the same nav works while in copy-mode.
192	
193	When `enableVimMode = false`, the entire 12-line block is omitted.
194	Consequence: `Ctrl+L` reaches the inner shell again (clears the
195	screen), `Ctrl+H` reaches readline as backspace, `Ctrl+J` is back to
196	LF (newline), `Ctrl+K` is back to readline's kill-line. **For
197	non-vim users this is the more conventional behavior**.
198	
199	Pane navigation is still possible via `prefix + h/j/k/l` (kept, see
200	next section) or `prefix + Arrow` (tmux default).
201	
202	**Documentation cross-link**: [`dot_config/television/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/television/config.toml)
203	removes its built-in `Ctrl+J/K` bindings to avoid conflict with
204	vim-tmux-navigator. That removal is **kept regardless of
205	`enableVimMode`** — vim-mode users would conflict, and non-vim users
206	don't lose anything because TV's `Ctrl+P/N` already handle next/prev.
207	
208	#### tmux — vim-letter pane select / resize (NOT gated)
209	
210	**File**: [`dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl) lines ~171–208.
211	
212	Three blocks are **NOT gated** by `enableVimMode`:
213	
214	- `prefix + h/j/k/l` → `select-pane -L/-D/-U/-R` (pane select)
215	- `prefix + H/J/K/L` → `resize-pane -L/-D/-U/-R 5` (resize 5 cells, repeatable)
216	- `prefix + M-h/j/k/l` → `resize-pane -L/-D/-U/-R 1` (fine resize, repeatable)
217	
218	Rationale: all three are prefix-gated, so they don't shadow anything
219	for non-vim users. They're "vim-letter shortcuts" but don't get in
220	anyone's way. Removing them would force non-vim users into
221	`prefix + Arrow`, which works but loses muscle-memory parity for users
222	who *do* know vim. Kept by deliberate decision.
223	
224	If you do want them gone too, edit `keybindings.conf.tmpl` and wrap
225	those three blocks in `{{ if .enableVimMode }}…{{ end }}`. The tmux
226	defaults `prefix + Arrow` for select and `prefix + Ctrl-Arrow` for
227	resize will take over.
228	
229	### Editor layer (none of these are gated)
230	
231	By design, **no editor's vim mode is gated** by `enableVimMode`. This
232	keeps the flag's meaning unambiguous: shells + tmux only.
233	
234	| Editor | What this repo manages | Vim mode? |
235	|---|---|---|
236	| Neovim (`dot_config/nvim/`) | LazyVim distro, lazy-lock, plugins, options | inherently vim — never disabled |
237	| VSCode (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/overlay.json` → various `dot_config/*/User/settings.json`) | font, line numbers, format-on-save | not managed; install `vscodevim.vim` extension manually if wanted |
238	| Cursor / Antigravity | same overlay as VSCode | not managed |
239	| Codex (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`) | model + tools settings | no vim-mode key managed |
240	| OpenCode (`dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`) | provider, leader key | no vim-mode key managed |
241	| Cursor-CLI (`dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) | provider, defaults | no vim-mode key managed |
242	
243	`editor.lineNumbers: "relative"` in the shared editor overlay is
244	vim-flavored display but not vim mode — kept regardless.
245	
246	**If you want VSCode-style vim** on opt-out machines, install the
247	`vscodevim.vim` extension manually. Don't try to gate it from this
248	repo's overlay — the overlay is shared across VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity
249	and the vim extension key would diverge between editors.
250	
251	### App layer
252	
253	#### marimo — `[keymap] preset = "vim"`
254	
255	**File**: [`dot_config/marimo/create_marimo.toml.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/marimo/create_marimo.toml.tmpl) line ~80.
256	
257	Marimo (Python notebook web UI) supports `[keymap] preset = "vim"` or
258	`"default"`. Templated to pick based on `enableVimMode`:
259	
260	```toml
261	[keymap]
262	destructive_delete = true
263	preset = "{{ if .enableVimMode }}vim{{ else }}default{{ end }}"
264	```
265	
266	**Caveat — `create_` semantics**: this file uses chezmoi's `create_`
267	prefix, which means chezmoi only seeds the file **once** (when the
268	target doesn't exist). It never re-touches the contents. So:
269	
270	- **Fresh install** → preset matches `enableVimMode` correctly.
271	- **Existing install** → preset stays whatever it was originally
272	  (probably `"vim"` since that was the historical default).
273	
274	If you flip `enableVimMode = false` on an existing machine and want
275	marimo to switch too, hand-edit `~/.config/marimo/marimo.toml` or
276	delete it and run `chezmoi apply` (which will re-seed with the new
277	template result).
278	
279	Why not `modify_` instead? Because marimo writes its own settings
280	(theme, recent files, snippet paths) into the same file via the web
281	UI, and a `modify_` script would have to reconcile those — overkill
282	for one keymap key.
283	
284	#### btop — `vim_keys` gated on `enableVimMode`
285	
286	**File**: [`dot_config/btop/create_btop.conf.tmpl`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/btop/create_btop.conf.tmpl) line ~25.
287	
288	btop (system monitor) exposes a `vim_keys` config key that enables
289	`h,j,k,l,g,G` directional control in its process / device lists
290	(the conflicting `h`→help and `k`→kill stay reachable with Shift).
291	Templated on `enableVimMode`:
292	
293	```ini
294	vim_keys = {{ if .enableVimMode }}True{{ else }}False{{ end }}
295	```
296	
297	**Caveat — `create_` semantics** (identical to marimo): the file is
298	seeded **once**; chezmoi never re-touches it, and btop rewrites the
299	whole config on every exit. Flipping `enableVimMode` later will
300	**not** re-flip `vim_keys` on an existing machine — delete
```

```text
1	# Custom fleet-hosts channel for television (tv).
2	# Sourced from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml — the same inventory used by
3	# `fleet chezmoi apply` / `fleet tmux` / `fleet info` / `fleet pueue` /
4	# `fleet exec`. Mirrors the `ssh-config` cable's UX but reads fleet's TOML
5	# inventory instead of ~/.ssh/config, so hosts with explicit
6	# hostname/user/port/identity_file (no ssh_alias) are reachable too.
7	#
8	# The actual TOML parsing lives in Python — this cable shells out to:
9	#   fleet hosts --list-tsv      (source — `name<TAB>target<TAB>kind` lines)
10	#   fleet hosts --describe N    (preview pane content)
11	#   fleet hosts N               (Enter action — os.execvp("ssh", ...))
12	# So this file stays small and the picker tracks any inventory changes
13	# automatically (no parallel TOML parser to keep in sync).
14	#
15	# Usage:
16	#   tv fleet-hosts
17	#   fleet hosts          # same picker via the fleet umbrella
18	#   fleet hosts lab-box  # skip the picker, SSH directly
19	#
20	# Keybindings (Alt+ namespace to avoid TV/tmux conflicts):
21	#   Enter      SSH into the selected host
22	#   Alt+T      BatchMode SSH probe (does passwordless login actually work?)
23	#   Alt+S      fleet chezmoi status scoped to this host
24	#   Alt+I      fleet info scoped to this host
25	#   Alt+P      fleet pueue scoped to this host
26	#   Ctrl+/     Toggle preview panel
27	#
28	# `local = true` hosts are intentionally hidden — they live on the
29	# orchestrator and have no SSH endpoint. Run `fleet hosts --list-tsv
30	# --include-local` to confirm one is in the inventory.
31	
32	[metadata]
33	name = "fleet-hosts"
34	description = "Fleet hosts (from ~/.config/fleet/machines.toml)"
35	requirements = ["fleet", "ssh"]
36	
37	[source]
38	command = "fleet hosts --list-tsv"
39	# Lines look like:   name<TAB>target<TAB>kind
40	# e.g.   lab-box <TAB> lab-box <TAB> alias:lab-box
41	#        vps-tokyo <TAB> 203.0.113.42 <TAB> explicit:dwlee@203.0.113.42
42	display = "{split:\\t:0}  ({split:\\t:2})"
43	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
44	
45	[preview]
46	command = "fleet hosts --describe '{split:\\t:0}'"
47	
48	[keybindings]
49	enter = "actions:connect"
50	alt-t = "actions:probe"
51	alt-s = "actions:status"
52	alt-i = "actions:info"
53	alt-p = "actions:pueue"
54	
55	[actions.connect]
56	description = "SSH into the selected fleet host"
57	command = "fleet hosts '{split:\\t:0}'"
58	mode = "execute"
59	
60	[actions.probe]
61	description = "BatchMode SSH probe (passwordless login check)"
62	command = "fleet hosts --probe '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
63	mode = "execute"
64	
65	[actions.status]
66	description = "fleet chezmoi status for this host"
67	command = "fleet chezmoi status --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
68	mode = "execute"
69	
70	[actions.info]
71	description = "fleet info for this host"
72	command = "fleet info --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
73	mode = "execute"
74	
75	[actions.pueue]
76	description = "fleet pueue for this host"
77	command = "fleet pueue --hosts '{split:\\t:0}'; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
78	mode = "execute"
79

1	# MLflow channel for television (tv).
2	# Browse experiments, runs, and registered models against any MLflow tracking
3	# backend (file:./mlruns, sqlite:///path/to/mlflow.db, or http://server:port).
4	#
5	# Usage:
6	#   tv mlflow
7	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow
8	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
9	#
10	# Prerequisites:
11	#   - `mlflow` installed (provided by dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools — the
12	#     CLI binary is what we exec under the `uv run --script` shebang of the
13	#     two helpers).
14	#   - `uv` on PATH (installed by uv role; required to resolve the PEP 723
15	#     inline-deps block in mlflow-source.py / mlflow-preview.py).
16	#
17	# Backend mode is resolved entirely from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI. When unset,
18	# mlflow 3.12+ auto-detects from $PWD: an `mlflow.db` file picks sqlite, an
19	# `mlruns/` dir picks file mode, otherwise it creates `mlruns/`. To pin a
20	# backend at launch time:
21	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://host:port tv mlflow
22	#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
23	#
24	# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
25	#   1. Experiments     all active experiments
26	#   2. Recent runs     top 50 runs across all experiments, by start_time desc
27	#   3. Runs (scoped)   runs in $MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID (hint row when unset;
28	#                      Alt+R on an experiment row sets it and re-launches tv)
29	#   4. Models          registered models from the model registry
30	#
31	# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
32	#   1. Full JSON       params, metrics, tags, artifact_uri, timestamps
33	#   2. Metrics-only    sorted key=value table; or aggregated across recent
34	#                      runs for an experiment row
35	#
36	# Keybindings:
37	#   Enter      Context-aware:
38	#                experiment row -> re-launch tv scoped to that experiment's
39	#                                  runs (nested drill-in; Esc exits the
40	#                                  drilled view back to the shell)
41	#                run / model row -> open full JSON detail in pager
42	#   Ctrl+Y     Copy id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard
43	#   Ctrl+O     Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only; prints a hint
44	#              otherwise)
45	#   Ctrl+B     Same as Ctrl+O — "B for browser" muscle-memory alias
46	#   Alt+R      Explicit drill — same as Enter on an experiment row,
47	#              available as a backup binding for muscle memory
48	#   Alt+J      Dump full JSON to terminal (paged)
49	#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview
50	#   Ctrl+S     Cycle source
51	#
52	# No `watch` field: mlflow imports are heavy (~1s warm, several seconds cold);
53	# experiments and runs change on the minute scale anyway. Press Ctrl+R to
54	# refresh manually after logging a new run.
55	#
56	# Hint row sentinel: when the backend is unreachable or a source is unscoped,
57	# the helper emits a single row with id `__hint__`. Real mlflow ids never
58	# collide (experiment_ids are non-negative ints; run_ids are 32-hex; model
59	# names cannot contain `__hint__` in practice).
60	
61	[metadata]
62	name = "mlflow"
63	description = "MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models (file/sqlite/http backends)"
64	requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]
65	
66	[source]
67	command = [
68	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments",
69	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent",
70	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment",
71	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models",
72	]
73	display = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  ({split:\\t:4})"
74	output = "{split:\\t:0}"
75	no_sort = true
76	
77	[preview]
78	# Helper always emits valid JSON now; pipe through `bat -l json` so the
79	# preview pane gets syntax highlighting (numbers, strings, keys). Same
80	# trick super-productivity.toml plays with `jq -C`, but bat's truecolor
81	# theme is easier on the eyes for nested objects.
82	#
83	# `--paging=never` is load-bearing: bat detects "not a TTY" inside TV's
84	# preview pipe and would otherwise still buffer; we want streamed output.
85	# `--plain` strips line numbers / decorations so the preview pane shows
86	# only the rendered content.
87	command = [
88	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full    | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
89	  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view metrics | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
90	]
91	header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"
92	
93	[ui]
94	input_header = "MLflow"
95	
96	[ui.preview_panel]
97	size = 60
98	
99	[keybindings]
100	enter = "actions:open-or-drill"
101	# Override TV's default ctrl-y (which copies the entire display row) with
102	# id-only copy. Matches super-productivity.toml's convention.
103	ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
104	ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"
105	# Ctrl+B is the muscle-memory alias — same action body as Ctrl+O. Reusing
106	# the existing action keeps the channel self-contained even if `mlf` (the
107	# umbrella CLI in dot_dotfiles/bin/) isn't installed.
108	ctrl-b = "actions:open-browser"
109	alt-r = "actions:drill-runs"
110	alt-j = "actions:dump-json"
111	
112	[actions.open-or-drill]
113	description = "Drill into experiment runs (experiment row) / open JSON detail (others)"
114	# Kind detection mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
115	#   __hint__       -> show the help JSON (helpful when MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is
116	#                     misconfigured: lets the user read the example URIs)
117	#   digit-only id  -> drill: re-exec tv with MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID + a
118	#                     --source-command override so the nested view shows ONLY
119	#                     this experiment's runs. Esc exits the drill back to
120	#                     the shell (TV does not have a back-stack; rerun
121	#                     `tv mlflow` for cross-experiment views).
122	#   anything else  -> open JSON detail in pager
123	#
124	# The header is set to "MLflow / <exp_name>" inside the drilled view so it's
125	# obvious you're in the nested context, not the top-level one. {split:\t:3}
126	# carries the experiment name in the experiments source layout (cols are:
127	# id, marker, lifecycle, name, last_update).
128	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
129	  __hint__) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
130	  *[!0-9]*) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
131	  *) MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" ;;
132	esac"""
133	mode = "execute"
134	
135	[actions.copy-id]
136	description = "Copy row id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard"
137	command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
138	mode = "fork"
139	
140	[actions.open-browser]
141	description = "Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only)"
142	# Build the URL inside the action so we read the live env var rather than
143	# baking it in. Inference mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
144	#   32-hex id -> need a roundtrip to find experiment_id, just open root
145	#   all-digit -> /#/experiments/<id>
146	#   else      -> /#/models/<name>
147	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; uri="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"; case "$uri" in http://*|https://*) ;; *) printf '[open-browser] needs MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http(s)://… — current: %s\\n' "${uri:-(unset)}"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$id" in __hint__) printf '[open-browser] no row selected\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; url="$uri/"; if [ "${#id}" = "32" ] && printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/0/runs/$id"; elif printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/$id"; else url="$uri/#/models/$id"; fi; if command -v open >/dev/null; then open "$url"; elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null; then xdg-open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 & elif command -v wslview >/dev/null; then wslview "$url"; else printf '[open-browser] no opener (open/xdg-open/wslview) — URL was: %s\\n' "$url"; sleep 2; fi"""
148	mode = "fork"
149	
150	[actions.drill-runs]
151	description = "Re-launch tv scoped to the highlighted experiment (Alt+R)"
152	# Same payload as the Enter drill branch — explicit binding for muscle
153	# memory and discoverability. No-op + hint on non-experiment rows so the
154	# user doesn't accidentally drill into an empty unscoped view.
155	command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
156	  __hint__|*[!0-9]*) printf '[drill-runs] not an experiment row (id=%s). Move to the Experiments source (Ctrl+S) and try again.\\n' "$id"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;;
157	esac
158	MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" """
159	mode = "execute"
160

163	command = "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"

1	# ~/.config/tmux/keybindings.conf
2	# All bind-key definitions and the prefix + Enter popup menu.

8	# is omitted entirely. See docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md.

12	# =============================================================================
13	# Mouse menu persistence
14	# =============================================================================
15	# tmux's built-in MouseDown3* bindings invoke display-menu without -O, so the
16	# menu dismisses the moment the right-click is released. Rebind with -O so the
17	# menu stays Open until an item is chosen or Escape is pressed.
18	
19	unbind-key -n MouseDown3Pane

21	# (keyboard equivalent is `prefix + M-p`, defined near the popup-menu section
22	# at the bottom of this file; the body is duplicated by design per
23	# pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md).
24	bind-key -n MouseDown3Pane \
25	  if-shell -F -t = "#{&&:#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},1,0},#{selection_present}}" \
26	    { send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel } \
27	    { if-shell -F -t = "#{||:#{mouse_any_flag},#{&&:#{pane_in_mode},#{?#{m/r:(copy|view)-mode,#{pane_mode}},0,1}}}" \
28	    { select-pane -t = ; send-keys -M } \
29	    { display-menu -O -T "#[align=centre]#{pane_current_command} (pane #{pane_index})" -t = -x M -y M \
30	        "Horizontal Split" h { split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}" } \
31	        "Vertical Split"   v { split-window -v -c "#{pane_current_path}" } \
32	        "" \
33	        "Swap Up"    u { swap-pane -U } \
34	        "Swap Down"  d { swap-pane -D } \
35	        "Swap Left"  l { swap-pane -t '{left-of}' } \
36	        "Swap Right" r { swap-pane -t '{right-of}' } \

54	unbind-key -n MouseDown3Status
55	# *** IF YOU EDIT THE MENU BODY, ALSO UPDATE dot_config/tmux/menu-window.sh ***
56	# (keyboard equivalent is `prefix + M-w`; body duplicated by design — see the
57	# comment above MouseDown3Pane for the pitfall reference.)
58	#
59	# Window-tab right-click menu.
60	#
61	# WARNING: this menu is currently 23 visible rows, well above the ~14-row
62	# soft cap documented in AGENTS.md ("tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu").
63	# tmux's display-menu silently suppresses itself if it can't fit on screen,
64	# so on small terminals (mobile SSH, half-height splits ~≤ 26 rows) the menu
65	# may not appear at all. Inlining (rather than nested submenus) is forced by
66	# pitfalls/tmux-submenu-flash-and-bottom-right.md — nested display-menu via
67	# run-shell from MouseDown3Status flashes / lands bottom-right / no-ops on
68	# second invocation. So everything stays flat here.

71	# tmux user-options:
72	#   - @bookmark_status — manual tag, toggled by ~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh
73	#   - @workmux_status  — agent state (🤖/💬/✅) written by workmux hooks; cleared
74	#                        here as the GUI equivalent of `wmclear` from 38_workmux.sh
75	# Both render side-by-side in the catppuccin window-text format (see

77	bind-key -n MouseDown3Status \

79	    "Swap Left"  l { swap-window -t :-1 } \

84	    "Main horizontal" 3 { select-layout main-horizontal } \
85	    "Main vertical"   4 { select-layout main-vertical } \

87	    "" \

89	    "Link to session..." K { choose-tree -Zs -F "#{session_name}" "link-window -s '#{window_id}' -t '%%:'" } \

99	    "🚩 Flag"     f { run-shell "~/.config/tmux/toggle-bookmark.sh '#{window_id}' '🚩'" } \
100	    "Clear agent status" c { set-option -w -t "#{window_id}" -u "@workmux_status" ; display-message "Cleared @workmux_status on #{window_index}:#{window_name}" } \
101	    "" \

131	# =============================================================================
132	# Vim-Style Copy Mode (prefix + [ to enter, q to exit)
133	# =============================================================================
134	#
135	#   h/j/k/l  move cursor        C-u/C-d  half-page up/down
136	#   g/G      top/bottom          //?      search forward/backward
137	#   v        begin selection     V        line selection
138	#   C-v      rectangle select    y        yank to clipboard
139	#   Escape   clear selection     q        exit copy mode
140	
141	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} v send-keys -X begin-selection
142	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} V send-keys -X select-line
143	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} C-v send-keys -X rectangle-toggle
144	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} y send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel
145	# Mouse drag = select-only (vim visual feel): highlight without copying, then `y`
146	# (copy-selection-and-cancel above) copies + exits. `stop-selection` keeps the
147	# highlight alive without leaving copy-mode. See docs/tools/tmux/.
148	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} MouseDragEnd1Pane send-keys -X stop-selection
149	# Double-click selects the word AND copies + exits (one gesture).
150	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} DoubleClick1Pane select-pane \; send-keys -X select-word \; send-keys -X copy-selection-and-cancel
151	
152	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
153	# Command-boundary navigation in copy-mode (Warp-style).
154	# Requires OSC 133 markers from the shell — emitted by
155	# dot_config/zsh/tools/02_shell_integration.zsh. In a plain shell (no markers,
156	# e.g. `sh`, `bash` without our hook, or `DISABLE_OSC133=1`), these keys are
157	# no-ops. tmux 3.4+ required for next-prompt/previous-prompt; the `-o` variant
158	# (jump to output start, not prompt start) is tmux 3.5+.
159	#
160	#   {  / }    previous/next prompt (the prompt line itself)
161	#   M-[ / M-] previous/next command output (line AFTER the prompt — usually
162	#             what you want for "skip to the output of the previous command")
163	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
164	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '{' send-keys -X previous-prompt
165	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} '}' send-keys -X next-prompt
166	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-[ send-keys -X previous-prompt -o
167	bind -T {{ $copyTable }} M-] send-keys -X next-prompt -o
168	
169	# =============================================================================
170	# Capture Pane Helpers
171	# =============================================================================
172	
173	# prefix + y: copy visible pane content to system clipboard
174	# `load-buffer -w -` loads into tmux's paste buffer AND forwards to the outer
175	# terminal via OSC 52 (requires `set-clipboard on` in common.conf). This works
176	# over SSH without shelling out to pbcopy/xclip on the remote host.
177	bind y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -p | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Pane content copied to clipboard'"
178	
179	# prefix + Y: copy full scrollback to system clipboard
180	bind Y run-shell "tmux capture-pane -pS - | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Full scrollback copied to clipboard'"

183	bind C-y run-shell "\
184	  tmux capture-pane -pS - | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% --multi --tac --no-sort \
185	    --header 'Select lines to copy (Tab=multi, Enter=copy)' \
186	    | tmux load-buffer -w - && tmux display-message 'Selected lines copied'"

189	# Requires OSC 133 markers — if the shell doesn't emit them (non-zsh shell,
190	# DISABLE_OSC133=1, or a remote bash without our hook), selection ends up
191	# empty. Chain: enter copy-mode, jump to start of previous command's output,
192	# begin selection, jump forward to the next prompt (end of output), copy,
193	# flash confirmation.
194	bind M-y copy-mode \; \
195	  send-keys -X previous-prompt -o \; \
196	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
197	  send-keys -X next-prompt \; \
198	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \

203	# (end-of-prompt), the copied text includes prompt chrome (e.g. "❯ echo hi"
204	# not just "echo hi"). Trim in the paste target if needed. Chain: enter
205	# copy-mode, jump to the previous prompt's A marker, begin selection, jump
206	# forward to the C marker (= start of output = end of input line), copy.
207	bind M-i copy-mode \; \
208	  send-keys -X previous-prompt \; \
209	  send-keys -X begin-selection \; \
210	  send-keys -X next-prompt -o \; \
211	  send-keys -X copy-pipe-and-cancel "tmux load-buffer -w -" \; \
212	  display-message "Last command input (prompt+line) copied to clipboard"
213	
214	# =============================================================================
215	# Vim-Style Pane Navigation
216	# =============================================================================
217	
218	bind h select-pane -L
219	bind j select-pane -D
220	bind k select-pane -U
221	bind l select-pane -R
222	
223	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
224	# vim-tmux-navigator: prefix-less Ctrl+h/j/k/l crosses tmux panes <-> vim splits
225	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
226	# Detect if the current pane is running vim/neovim; if so forward the key,
227	# otherwise move between tmux panes. Matches christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator.
228	# Gated on chezmoi `enableVimMode` (default true). When off, Ctrl+h/j/k/l
229	# pass through to the inner shell (Ctrl+L = clear, Ctrl+H = backspace, etc.).
230	# See docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md.
231	{{ if .enableVimMode -}}
232	is_vim="ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}' | grep -iqE '^[^TXZ ]+ +(\\S+\\/)?g?\\.?(view|n?vim?x?)(-wrapped)?(diff)?$'"
233	bind-key -n 'C-h' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-h'  'select-pane -L'
234	bind-key -n 'C-j' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-j'  'select-pane -D'
235	bind-key -n 'C-k' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-k'  'select-pane -U'
236	bind-key -n 'C-l' if-shell "$is_vim" 'send-keys C-l'  'select-pane -R'
237	# NOTE: C-\ (select-pane -l) removed — tmux 3.4+ cannot parse C-\ in config files.
238	# Use directional C-h/j/k/l instead, or prefix+; for last-pane.
239	
240	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-h' select-pane -L
241	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-j' select-pane -D
242	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-k' select-pane -U
243	bind-key -T copy-mode-vi 'C-l' select-pane -R
244	{{- else -}}
245	# enableVimMode = false: vim-tmux-navigator omitted. Use prefix + h/j/k/l
246	# (kept below) or prefix + Arrow for pane navigation.
247	{{- end }}
248	
249	# Intuitive split bindings (| = left/right, - = top/bottom)
250	bind | split-window -h -c "#{pane_current_path}"

1	# Per-project workspace layout
2	#
3	# Generic layout for any code repo. Use via sesh wildcard
4	# (~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml: pattern = "/Volumes/Data/Program/*/*"), or
5	# directly — the yaml has no `start_directory:` (see note below), so the
6	# pane's cwd at invocation time controls where windows land:
7	#
8	#   cd ~/some/repo && tmuxp load -a -y ~/.config/tmuxp/project.yaml
9	#
10	# Windows:
11	#   1. editor   — nvim (full pane)
12	#   2. shell    — interactive shell at project root
13	#   3. git      — lazygit (only if `lazygit` binary exists; otherwise plain git status)
14	#
15	# Why no horizontal splits in `editor`:
16	#   nvim's :terminal + tmux navigator already covers in-editor terminal needs.
17	#   Keeping `editor` single-pane lets nvim use full width for tree+code+sidebar.
18	#   For coding-agent layouts (nvim | specstory) use the dedicated
19	#   ~/.config/tmuxp/coding-agent.yaml — that's the persistent agent workspace,
20	#   this template is the per-repo workhorse.
21	
22	session_name: project
23	# No session-level `start_directory:` on purpose. Two tmuxp traps make
24	# every "obvious" value wrong in append mode (which is how sesh uses us):
25	#   1. `${VAR:-default}` isn't expanded by Python's `os.path.expandvars`,
26	#      so it's passed literally to `tmux new-window -c` → invalid path →
27	#      tmux silently falls back to $HOME for every window.
28	#   2. `.` / `./foo` ARE resolved, but relative to the YAML file's
29	#      directory (tmuxp/cli/load.py:359), not to tmuxp's process cwd —
30	#      so windows would land in `~/.config/tmuxp/`, not the repo.
31	# With no `start_directory` in the yaml, libtmux omits `-c` on
32	# `tmux new-window`, and tmux inherits the calling pane's cwd. The sesh
33	# `startup_command` (~/.config/sesh/sesh.toml) does `cd {} && tmuxp load
34	# -a …` from inside the pane, so "calling pane's cwd" IS the matched
35	# repo path. See pitfalls/tmuxp-append-ignores-session-start-directory.md.
36	
37	windows:
38	  - window_name: editor
39	    panes:
40	      - shell_command: nvim
41	
42	  - window_name: shell
43	    panes:
44	      - shell_command: ""
45	
46	  - window_name: git
47	    panes:
48	      - shell_command: |
49	          if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
50	            lazygit
51	          else
52	            git status
53	          fi
54
```

2	# /// script

6	# ]
7	# ///
8	"""tmux-session-summary — AI-powered overview of every tmux session.
9	
10	Subcommands:
11	  list      Human-readable summary, one block per session (default).
12	  picker    TSV `<session>\\t<one-line>` for fzf. Used by `tsum -i` and the
13	            tmux popup menu entry.
14	
15	Flags:
16	  -d, --deep        Include the visible area (20-100 lines) of each session's
17	                    active pane in the LLM prompt. More context, more tokens,
18	                    may include scrollback content. Self-capture is skipped
19	                    automatically (the pane running tsum is excluded).
20	  --shallow         Force metadata-only mode (overrides TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT).
21	  -r, --refresh     Bypass the prompt-hash cache; force a fresh LLM call.
22	  --dry-run         Print the constructed prompt to stdout and exit (no API
23	                    call). Lets you audit what would be sent.
24	  --no-cache        Don't read or write the cache (one-off invocation).
25	  --sort {alpha,closability}
26	                    alpha (default): tmux's natural order (alphabetical).
27	                    closability: keep → check → safe, so active work surfaces
28	                    first.
29	  --only {safe,check,keep}
30	                    Filter to one tier only. Combine with picker mode to bulk
31	                    inspect candidates: `tsum picker --only safe | fzf -m`.
32	
33	Deep-by-default:
34	  Set `TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT=1` (e.g. in ~/.shellrc.adhoc) to make --deep implicit;
35	  override per-invocation with --shallow. CLI flags always win over the env
36	  var: --deep beats --shallow beats TSUM_DEEP_DEFAULT beats metadata-only.
37	
38	Env vars (mirrors dot_config/zsh/tools/04_ai_capture.zsh — set in your
39	shell rc to override globally):
40	
41	  AICAP_AGENT             auto | claude | opencode | codex | cursor-agent | http
42	  AICAP_CLAUDE_MODEL      default: haiku
43	  AICAP_OPENCODE_MODEL    default: github-copilot/claude-haiku-4.5
44	  AICAP_CODEX_MODEL       default: gpt-5-mini
45	  AICAP_CURSOR_MODEL      default: (let cursor-agent pick)
46	  AICAP_HTTP_URL          default: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions
47	  AICAP_HTTP_MODEL        default: google/gemini-2.0-flash-exp:free
48	  AICAP_HTTP_API_KEY      default: $OPENROUTER_API_KEY
49	  TSUM_MIN_REFRESH_INTERVAL  seconds, default 120. Throttle window when the
50	                          prompt hash changes — within it, reuse the stale
51	                          cache to absorb high-frequency churn (htop, watch,
52	                          progress bars). Identical-prompt hits ignore this
53	                          and reuse the cache regardless of age. Set to 0
54	                          to disable throttling. TSUM_CACHE_TTL accepted as
55	                          a fallback alias for back-compat.
56	  TSUM_TIMEOUT            seconds, default 60 (LLM call timeout)
57	  TSUM_TMUX_BIN           full path to tmux binary, default "tmux" — set this
58	                          when multiple tmux versions are on PATH and the
59	                          server you want runs from a specific one (apt vs
60	                          appimage protocol mismatch). E.g. /bin/tmux.
61

90	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
91	# SSOT loader — parse dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh so this script gets
92	# the same AICAP_* defaults as aifix/aiblock without redeclaring them. Used
93	# only when env vars aren't already inherited (cron, tmux popup, etc.).
94	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
95	_SSOT_PATH_CANDIDATES = (
96	    "~/.config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh",
97	    # When run from the chezmoi source dir before `chezmoi apply`:
98	    "~/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/shell/04_ai_agents.sh",
99	)
100	# Match `: "${VAR:=value}"` lines — value may be empty or contain spaces.
101	# Captures: (var_name, raw_value)
102	_SSOT_LINE = re.compile(r'^\s*:\s*"\$\{(AICAP_\w+):=([^}]*)\}"\s*$')
103	
104	
105	def _load_ssot_defaults() -> dict[str, str]:
106	    """Return AICAP_* defaults parsed from the first existing SSOT path.
107	
108	    Empty dict if no candidate exists — callers should fall back to the
109	    hardcoded safety defaults below. Drift between this script and the
110	    shell file is impossible because we read the file at process start.
111	    """
112	    for raw in _SSOT_PATH_CANDIDATES:
113	        p = Path(os.path.expanduser(raw))
114	        if not p.is_file():
115	            continue
116	        out: dict[str, str] = {}
117	        try:
118	            for line in p.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
119	                m = _SSOT_LINE.match(line)
120	                if m:
121	                    out[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
122	        except OSError:
123	            return {}
124	        return out
125	    return {}

128	_SSOT = _load_ssot_defaults()

131	def _env_or_ssot(key: str, hardcoded_fallback: str = "") -> str:
132	    """Resolution order: env var (live override) > SSOT file > hardcoded
133	    safety default. The hardcoded value should only kick in on hosts that
134	    have neither inherited the env nor deployed the SSOT — a rare edge."""
135	    val = os.environ.get(key)
136	    if val is not None:  # explicitly set (even to empty) wins
137	        return val
138	    return _SSOT.get(key, hardcoded_fallback)

145	# Hardcoded values below are safety fallbacks only — they kick in when both
146	# the env var is unset AND the SSOT file is missing (e.g. an unpacked
147	# tarball without `chezmoi apply`). The drift risk vs the SSOT is contained

243	def _tmux(*args: str, timeout: float = 5.0) -> str:
244	    """Run `$TSUM_TMUX_BIN ARGS...` and return stdout. Empty string on failure
245	    (stderr captured in _LAST_TMUX_STDERR for diagnostic surfacing)."""
246	    global _LAST_TMUX_STDERR

292	        if deep:

294	                name, sess.windows, my_pane

150	if-shell 'tmux -V | grep -qE "tmux ([3-9]\.[5-9]|[3-9]\.[1-9][0-9]|[4-9]\.)"' \

154	# OSC 52 clipboard (works over SSH)

156	
157	# Declare OSC 52 support explicitly for common outer terminals. tmux 3.2+ only
158	# emits OSC 52 when it believes the outer terminal supports it; most modern
159	# terminals (Ghostty, Alacritty, iTerm2, kitty, WezTerm) do. Without these
160	# hints tmux falls back to terminfo's `Ms` capability, which is absent from
161	# the `tmux-256color` entry shipped by many distros, so yanks from inner
162	# apps (e.g. Neovim over SSH) silently drop.

```text
1	# tmux + OSC 133 capture helpers — shell-level counterparts of the
2	# prefix + M-y / M-i tmux bindings, with an N-back index.
3	#
4	#   cpcmd [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT  (zsh history; universal)
5	#   cpout [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT (tmux copy-mode chain)
6	#   cpblock [N]  last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK, Warp-style
7	#
8	# N defaults to 1 (= latest). N=2 is the one before that, and so on.
9	#
10	# Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`)
11	# AND copies to system clipboard. Diagnostic + byte count go to stderr so
12	# stdout stays clean for pipes.
13	#
14	# WHY cpout/cpblock need tmux:
15	# tmux consumes OSC 133 marker bytes and only stores them as per-line
16	# attributes in its grid — `tmux capture-pane -pe` does NOT re-emit them.
17	# Outside tmux there's no portable way to recover boundaries of a past
18	# command's output (terminals like iTerm2/Ghostty have proprietary APIs,
19	# but nothing cross-terminal). cpcmd uses zsh shell history instead, so it
20	# works universally.
21	#
22	# Requires: zsh; plus tmux for cpout/cpblock.
23	
24	# Pipe stdin to system clipboard, preferring tmux's OSC 52 bridge (SSH-safe)
25	# and falling back to platform-native clipboard tools.
26	_cpx_to_clipboard() {
27	  if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
28	    tmux load-buffer -w -
29	  elif command -v pbcopy &>/dev/null; then
30	    pbcopy
31	  elif command -v wl-copy &>/dev/null; then
32	    wl-copy
33	  elif command -v xclip &>/dev/null; then
34	    xclip -selection clipboard -in
35	  elif command -v xsel &>/dev/null; then
36	    xsel --clipboard --input
37	  else
38	    cat >/dev/null
39	    return 1
40	  fi
41	}
42	
43	# Validate a positive-integer argument. Echoes the value on success; prints
44	# a usage hint to stderr and returns 1 on invalid input.
45	_cpx_parse_n() {
46	  local name=$1 n=${2:-1}
47	  if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
48	    print -u2 "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n). Usage: $name [N]"
49	    return 1
50	  fi
51	  print -r -- "$n"
52	}
53	
54	# Run a tmux copy-mode selection chain on the current pane. Prints selection
55	# to stdout, diagnostic (name + byte count) to stderr. Returns 1 on empty.
56	#
57	#   _cpx_tmux_select <display-name> <prev-count> <prev-cmd> [prev-args...]
58	#
59	# Chain: copy-mode → (<prev-cmd> <prev-args...>) × <prev-count> →
60	#        begin-selection → next-prompt →
61	#        copy-pipe-and-cancel "tee <tmp> | tmux load-buffer -w -" → wait-for
62	#
63	# <prev-count> is how many times to repeat the `previous-*` command before
64	# starting the selection — that's how N-back lookback is done.
65	#
66	# Depends on 02_shell_integration.zsh skipping the OSC 133 C marker for
67	# these helpers' own invocation (see the case statement there). Without
68	# that skip, `previous-prompt -o` would land on this command's own output
69	# start and the selection would be empty.
70	_cpx_tmux_select() {
71	  local name=$1; shift
72	  local prev_count=$1; shift
73	  local tmp sentinel i _y
74	  tmp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/cpx-$$-$RANDOM"
75	  sentinel="cpx-$$-$RANDOM"
76	  : > "$tmp"
77	  tmux copy-mode -t "$TMUX_PANE" 2>/dev/null || return 1
78	  # Seek to history bottom so N-back math is measured from a known origin.
79	  tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X history-bottom 2>/dev/null
80	  # Sync barrier between `send-keys -X` calls: an assignment from
81	  # `$(tmux display-message -p …)` is what actually forces the tmux server
82	  # to commit the previous copy-mode command before it answers. Without
83	  # this round-trip, bursts of `previous-prompt` calls collapse to a single
84	  # cursor jump on tmux 3.6a — `sleep`, `: "$(…)"`, and bare redirection
85	  # (`>/dev/null`) are ALL insufficient. The variable read is what makes zsh
86	  # wait for subprocess output, which in turn serialises tmux's queue.
87	  for (( i = 0; i < prev_count; i++ )); do
88	    tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X "$@" 2>/dev/null
89	    _y=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" '#{copy_cursor_y}' 2>/dev/null)
90	  done
91	  tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X begin-selection 2>/dev/null
92	  tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X next-prompt 2>/dev/null
93	  _y=$(tmux display-message -p -t "$TMUX_PANE" '#{copy_cursor_y}' 2>/dev/null)
94	  tmux send-keys -t "$TMUX_PANE" -X copy-pipe-and-cancel \
95	    "tee $tmp | tmux load-buffer -w - ; tmux wait-for -S $sentinel" 2>/dev/null
96	  tmux wait-for "$sentinel" 2>/dev/null
97	  if [[ -s "$tmp" ]]; then
98	    cat "$tmp"
99	    local bytes
100	    bytes=$(wc -c <"$tmp" | tr -d ' ')
101	    rm -f "$tmp"
102	    print -u2 "$name: $bytes bytes copied to clipboard"
103	    return 0
104	  fi
105	  rm -f "$tmp"
106	  return 1
107	}
108	
109	# cpcmd [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT. Universal: reads zsh
110	# shell history. Clean output (no prompt chrome, no terminal-echo artefacts).
111	cpcmd() {
112	  emulate -L zsh
113	  local n
114	  n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpcmd "${1:-1}") || return 1
115	  local cmd
116	  # fc -ln -N -N: list entries from (-N) to (-N), inclusive — just the Nth back
117	  cmd=$(fc -ln -"$n" -"$n" 2>/dev/null)
118	  cmd="${cmd#	}"   # strip fc's leading tab
119	  cmd="${cmd# }"
120	  if [[ -z "$cmd" ]]; then
121	    print -u2 "cpcmd: no command at N=$n in shell history"
122	    return 1
123	  fi
124	  printf '%s\n' "$cmd" | _cpx_to_clipboard || {
125	    print -u2 "cpcmd: no clipboard tool available (install pbcopy / xclip / xsel / wl-copy, or run inside tmux)"
126	    return 1
127	  }
128	  printf '%s\n' "$cmd"
129	  print -u2 "cpcmd: ${#cmd} bytes (zsh history -$n) copied to clipboard"
130	}
131	
132	# cpout [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT via tmux's OSC 133 line
133	# attrs. cpout/cpcmd/cpblock themselves are preexec-skipped for C, so N=1
134	# lands on the *previous* command's output start, N=2 on the one before, etc.
135	cpout() {
136	  emulate -L zsh
137	  if [[ -z "$TMUX" ]]; then
138	    print -u2 "cpout: requires tmux (OSC 133 boundaries are stored per-pane by tmux). Use cpcmd for input, or your terminal's native 'copy output' if available."
139	    return 1
140	  fi
141	  local n
142	  n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpout "${1:-1}") || return 1
143	  _cpx_tmux_select "cpout -$n" "$n" previous-prompt -o || {
144	    print -u2 "cpout: empty at N=$n — (a) shell pre-dates chezmoi apply, run 'exec zsh' (verify: echo \$precmd_functions | grep osc133); (b) N exceeds command history in this pane; (c) target command is an alt-screen TUI (vim, htop) with no OSC 133 output."
145	    return 1
146	  }
147	}
148	
149	# cpblock [N] — last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK (prompt + input +
150	# output), Warp-style. The OSC 133 A marker is embedded in PROMPT itself
151	# (02_shell_integration.zsh) so cpblock's OWN prompt carries an A too —
152	# call previous-prompt N+1 times to skip self + land N-back.
153	cpblock() {
154	  emulate -L zsh
155	  if [[ -z "$TMUX" ]]; then
156	    print -u2 "cpblock: requires tmux (see cpout for why)."
157	    return 1
158	  fi
159	  local n
160	  n=$(_cpx_parse_n cpblock "${1:-1}") || return 1
161	  _cpx_tmux_select "cpblock -$n" $(( n + 1 )) previous-prompt || {
162	    print -u2 "cpblock: empty at N=$n — run 'exec zsh' if the shell pre-dates chezmoi apply, or N exceeds command history in this pane."
163	    return 1
164	  }
165	}
166

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# ~/.config/tmux/responsive.sh
3	# Build per-client adaptive Catppuccin status bar.
4	#
5	# tmux evaluates status-left/status-right ONCE per client per refresh, so
6	# #{client_width} inside the format expands to *that* client's width. We
7	# build three module bundles (wide/medium/narrow) into user options, then
8	# write a status-right whose top-level conditional picks the bundle based
9	# on the rendering client's width.
10	#
11	# Width tiers (per client):
12	#   >= 120  (wide)   : application + user + host + date_time
13	#   80-119  (medium) : host + date_time
14	#   < 80    (narrow) : empty
15	#
16	# Called once at startup. No client-resized hook needed -- the format
17	# itself reacts to each client's width on every status refresh.
18	
19	set -euo pipefail
20	
21	# -- Module bundles (stored as user options so the format can reference them)
22	#
23	# IMPORTANT: use `set -gq` (NOT `-gqF`) to store the module references as
24	# *unexpanded* strings. The status-left/status-right format below then wraps
25	# the lookup in a single `#{E:...}` expansion.
26	#
27	# session is hand-rolled instead of using `#{E:@catppuccin_status_session}`
28	# because catppuccin's session module stores `#{E:@catppuccin_session_text}`
29	# (which expands to `#S`) inside its own variable via `set -ag` (not `-agF`).
30	# This creates triple-nested `#{E:}` expansion that tmux's format cache does
31	# not invalidate on `client-session-changed`, leaving the old session name
32	# in status-left after `tmux switch-client` / `sesh connect` until manual
33	# `prefix + R` reload. See catppuccin/tmux#337.
34	#
35	# We replicate the catppuccin look (colour pill + text) using the same
36	# `@thm_*` palette variables, but with a literal `#S` so tmux re-renders it
37	# every status refresh.
38	# session pill changes colour green->red on prefix (built-in client_prefix
39	# tracking). That colour shift is enough indication; we tried adding a
40	# separate `⌨ PFX` flag but it duplicated information already conveyed by
41	# the pill colour change.
42	_session_block='#[fg=#{?client_prefix,#{E:@thm_red},#{E:@thm_green}}]#{E:@catppuccin_status_left_separator}#[fg=#{E:@thm_crust},bg=#{?client_prefix,#{E:@thm_red},#{E:@thm_green}}] #[fg=#{E:@thm_fg},bg=#{E:@thm_surface_0}] #S#[fg=#{E:@thm_surface_0},bg=default]#{E:@catppuccin_status_right_separator}'
43	
44	tmux set -gq '@_status_right_wide' \
45	  '#{E:@catppuccin_status_application}#{E:@catppuccin_status_user}#{E:@catppuccin_status_host}#{E:@catppuccin_status_date_time}'
46	tmux set -gq '@_status_right_medium' \
47	  '#{E:@catppuccin_status_host}#{E:@catppuccin_status_date_time}'
48	tmux set -gq '@_status_right_narrow' ''
49	
50	tmux set -gq '@_status_left_wide' \
51	  "${_session_block}#{E:@catppuccin_status_directory}"
52	tmux set -gq '@_status_left_narrow' \
53	  "${_session_block}"
54	
55	# -- Per-client status-right: pick bundle by client_width.
56	#    e|>=: numeric comparison; nested #{?:,:} is fine here because each
57	#    branch is a single #{E:@_status_right_*} reference (no commas inside).
58	tmux set -g status-right \

1	#!/usr/bin/env zsh
2	# scode-here — open the repo-aware coding-agent layout (`scode`) for the
3	# directory passed as $1 (typically tmux's #{pane_current_path}).
4	#
5	# Bound to `prefix + 9` in dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf. Lives in its
6	# own file because:
7	#   1. tmux run-shell uses /bin/sh and can't see zsh functions/aliases. We
8	#      need an explicit zsh subshell that sources the helper.
9	#   2. The session-name + switch-client logic is non-trivial enough that
10	#      inlining it in keybindings.conf risks the same kind of quoting trap
11	#      as the display-menu case (see pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail).
12	#   3. Easier to debug — `tmux display-message` errors come back via
13	#      $TMUX_LOG below.
14	#
15	# scode itself walks up to find .git via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`,
16	# so any directory inside a repo works. Outside any repo, scode errors and
17	# we surface that to the tmux status line.
18	#
19	# scode is idempotent: calling it again from inside the same repo just
20	# switches to the existing `coding-agent/<repo>` session.
21	
22	set -eu
23	
24	target_dir="${1:-$PWD}"
25	log="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tmux-scode-here.log"
26	
27	# Source the helper. ZDOTDIR is respected by chezmoi-managed zsh setup.
28	HELPER="${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME/.config/zsh}/tools/22_sesh.zsh"
29	if [[ ! -r "$HELPER" ]]; then
30	    tmux display-message "scode-here: helper not found at $HELPER"
31	    exit 1
32	fi
33	
34	# shellcheck disable=SC1090
35	source "$HELPER"
36	
37	# Build the session in the background; sesh-code prints diagnostics on
38	# stderr if something fails (not a repo, missing tools, etc).
39	if ! sesh-code --no-attach -p "$target_dir" >"$log" 2>&1; then
40	    err="$(tail -n 1 "$log" 2>/dev/null || echo "(see $log)")"
41	    tmux display-message "scode failed: $err"
42	    exit 1
43	fi
44	
45	# Compute the session name the same way sesh-code does, so we can switch.
46	# _sesh_sanitize and _sesh_git_root are sourced from the helper above.
47	repo_root="$(cd "$target_dir" && _sesh_git_root)"
48	session="coding-agent/$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$repo_root")")"
49	
50	if ! tmux switch-client -t "$session" 2>>"$log"; then
51	    tmux display-message "scode created '$session' but switch-client failed (see $log)"
52	    exit 1
53	fi
54
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Smart picker — unified entry point for tmux session / project / worktree switching.
3	#
4	# Invoked from:
5	#   - tmux:       bind-key "g" run-shell '~/.config/tmux/smart-picker.sh'
6	#   - tmux menu:  menu.sh → "Sesh picker" row
7	#   - zsh ZLE:    sesh-sessions widget (Alt+S), via 22_sesh.zsh
8	#
9	# Source filter hotkeys inside the popup (muscle memory inherited from the
10	# previous sesh-picker.sh — ^w is the new addition):
11	#   ^a all         sesh list --icons
12	#   ^t tmux        sesh list -t --icons (active tmux sessions)
13	#   ^g configs     sesh list -c --icons
14	#   ^x zoxide      sesh list -z --icons (frecency dirs)
15	#   ^w worktrees   this script --list-worktrees (current repo's worktrees)
16	#   ^f find        fd walk from $HOME (depth 2)
17	#   ^d kill        kill the tmux session under cursor, then reload
18	#
19	# Smart dispatch on Enter (Case order matters — first match wins):
20	#   1. Existing tmux session name   → sesh connect (sesh handles switch/attach)
21	#   2. Path inside a git repo       → scode -p <path> (coding-agent layout)
22	#   3. Path NOT inside a git repo   → sesh connect (plain; honors wildcards)
23	#   4. Configured sesh session name → sesh connect (honors startup_command)
24	#
25	# Why call `scode` (zsh function) from bash: the existing scode handles all
26	# the per-repo session naming + layout + specstory wrapping. Reinventing it
27	# here would drift. `zsh -ic` sources zshrc → defines the alias → runs it.
28	#
29	# ANSI handling: sesh list --icons emits ANSI color codes. fzf --ansi renders
30	# them correctly, but the returned string still contains them. `sesh connect`
31	# tolerates ANSI-tainted input (it has for months), but our own path-vs-name
32	# check below strips ANSI before inspecting.
33	
34	set -euo pipefail
35	
36	SCRIPT_PATH="${BASH_SOURCE[0]:-$0}"
37	# Resolve to absolute path so fzf's reload(...) subshells find us reliably.
38	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$SCRIPT_PATH")" && pwd)"
39	SCRIPT_ABS="${SCRIPT_DIR}/$(basename "$SCRIPT_PATH")"
40	
41	# ── Worktree source ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
42	# MVP: list worktrees of the current working directory's repo only. `git
43	# worktree list --porcelain` is stable, doesn't require worktrunk, and matches
44	# what `wt list` would show for the current project. No output if not in a
45	# repo — the picker just renders an empty list for ^w in that case.
46	list_worktrees() {
47	    git worktree list --porcelain 2>/dev/null |
48	        awk '/^worktree / { print "🌲 " $2 }'
49	}
50	
51	if [[ "${1:-}" == "--list-worktrees" ]]; then
52	    list_worktrees
53	    exit 0
54	fi
55	
56	# ── Picker ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
57	selected="$(
58	    sesh list --icons | fzf-tmux -p 80%,70% \
59	        --no-sort --ansi \
60	        --border-label ' smart ' \
61	        --prompt '⚡  ' \
62	        --header '  ^a all ^t tmux ^g configs ^x zoxide ^w worktrees ^f find ^d kill' \
63	        --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
64	        --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
65	        --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
66	        --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
67	        --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \
68	        --bind "ctrl-w:change-prompt(🌲  )+reload(${SCRIPT_ABS} --list-worktrees)" \
69	        --bind 'ctrl-f:change-prompt(🔎  )+reload(fd -H -d 2 -t d -E .Trash . ~)' \
70	        --bind 'ctrl-d:execute(tmux kill-session -t {2..})+change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
71	        --preview-window 'right:55%' \
72	        --preview 'sesh preview {}'
73	)" || exit 0
74	
75	[[ -z "$selected" ]] && exit 0
76	
77	# ── Dispatch ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
78	# Strip ANSI escape codes for inspection. $'\033' is the ESC literal; works
79	# on both GNU sed (Linux) and BSD sed (macOS).
80	esc=$'\033'

```text
# Herdr Agent State Detection & Integration

## State Detection Mechanism

Herdr uses a **dual-layered detection system**:

1. **Automatic Screen Manifest Detection**: For agents without complete lifecycle hooks, Herdr reads the "live bottom-buffer screen snapshot" and evaluates TOML manifests against it to classify `idle`, `working`, and `blocked`. This includes matching terminal titles and OSC progress sequences.

2. **Explicit Hook/Plugin Reporting**: Agents with complete lifecycle hooks (like Pi or Kimi Code CLI when installed) report state directly. The integration becomes "authoritative when actively reporting for the running pane."

## Claude Code Specific Behavior

Claude Code uses **screen manifest detection only**—its integration intentionally isn't a lifecycle authority. This means Herdr visually observes Claude Code's terminal UI rather than receiving direct state reports. The system can "match terminal title and progress (OSC) sequences as detection evidence."

## Explicit State Reporting Options

Agents can report status via two mechanisms:

**CLI Command** (for custom status labels):
```
herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --source custom:indexer --agent docs-bot --state working --custom-status indexing
```

**Socket API**: Agents with complete lifecycle hooks emit state reports through the socket API when installed.

## UI Status Indication

The sidebar performs "state rollups"—a blocked agent makes its pane/tab/workspace appear blocked; a working agent marks the workspace as active. This creates the workflow: "start several agents, let them work in parallel, and use the sidebar to see which project needs a decision."

## CLI Commands for Agent Management

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `herdr agent start reviewer -- claude` | Spawn an agent in Herdr |
| `herdr agent attach reviewer` | Direct terminal attachment |
| `herdr agent explain <target>` | Debug state detection |
| `herdr agent list` | View tracked agents |
| `herdr agent rename w1:p1 reviewer` | Custom labels |
```

7	#   sesh-code / scode   — repo-scoped `coding-agent/<repo>` layout
8	#                         (nvim 75% | agent 25%, btop monitor window)
9	#   sesh-vibe / svibe   — parametric multi-agent vibe layout
10	#                         (N agent panes + lazygit + nvim windows)
11	#   sesh-sessions       — fzf-tmux picker over `sesh list`
12	#

14	#   zsh : ZLE widget + bindkey '\es'        → dot_config/zsh/tools/22_sesh.zsh
15	#   bash: ble.sh `ble-bind -x 'M-s'`         → dot_config/bash/06_sesh.bash.tmpl

25	# ble-bind callback both just invoke this. Prompt redraw on exit is handled

35	            --bind 'tab:down,btab:up' \
36	            --bind 'ctrl-a:change-prompt(⚡  )+reload(sesh list --icons)' \
37	            --bind 'ctrl-t:change-prompt(🪟  )+reload(sesh list -t --icons)' \
38	            --bind 'ctrl-g:change-prompt(⚙️  )+reload(sesh list -c --icons)' \
39	            --bind 'ctrl-x:change-prompt(📁  )+reload(sesh list -z --icons)' \

1	# tmux Cheatsheet
2	
3	> **Prefix** = `Ctrl + b` · Press inside tmux: `prefix + Space` for menu, `prefix + ?` for fuzzy key search.
4	
5	## Most-Used (memorize these first)
6	
7	| Key | Action |
8	|-----|--------|
9	| `prefix + Space` | Popup menu (script-driven, height-aware, with submenus) |
10	| `prefix + ?` | **fzf** picker over ALL keybindings (tmux-fzf) |
11	| `prefix + /` | Prompt for a key, show what it's bound to |

```text
# herdr-plus Plugin Overview

## Core Functionality

herdr-plus is a first-class herdr plugin adding two major capabilities:

1. **Projects** — declarative workspace templates allowing users to spin up complex multi-tab, multi-pane environments with a single keystroke via fuzzy picker
2. **Quick Actions** — a fuzzy launcher for running one-off scripts and commands from any directory

## Key Features

**Projects** support:
- TOML-based configuration files stored in `projects/` subdirectory
- Up to 4 panes per tab with customizable splits (vertical/horizontal)
- Optional grouping to organize related projects under headings
- Variable expansion for paths (~ and $ENV support)

**Quick Actions** support:
- Three action types: command, select (fuzzy second list), and form (user input)
- Go template rendering with context variables (WorkDir, SessionTitle, Value, etc.)
- Project-level actions in `<repo>/.herdr-plus/quick-actions/`
- Global actions in plugin config directory

**Worktree auto-layout**:
- Automatically applies tab layouts when herdr creates or opens git worktrees
- Matches layouts by repository name and optional branch specification
- Fires on `worktree.created` and `worktree.opened` events

## Installation & Usage

Installation via plugin system: `herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`

The plugin is also available as a standalone binary through Homebrew or installation script.

Key bindings are configured manually in herdr's `config.toml` using action IDs:
- `cloudmanic.herdr-plus.projects`
- `cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions`

Configuration persists in `~/.config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/`
```

## SUMMARY: TMUX DEPENDENCIES FOR HERDR MIGRATION

| Feature | Tmux API Used | Portability Risk | Notes |
|---------|---------------|------------------|-------|
| **Per-window user-options** | `tmux set-option -w '@<name>'` | **HIGH** | No equivalent in most multiplexers; requires custom state storage |
| **Format-string interpolation** | `#{@option}`, `#{?@option, ...}` | **HIGH** | Powerful but tmux-specific; alternatives may not have equivalent |
| **Window-status format** | `set window-status-format` + `#{window_name}` + custom vars | **HIGH** | Theme plugin architecture is tmux-specific |
| **Copy-mode tables** | `copy-mode-vi` vs `copy-mode` + `send-keys -X` | **MEDIUM** | Selectable copy modes exist; actions are portable (vi/emacs) |
| **Mode-keys setting** | `set mode-keys vi|emacs` | **MEDIUM** | Most multiplexers support both; switching is straightforward |
| **Extended keys (CSI-u)** | `set extended-keys on` + `terminal-features` | **MEDIUM** | Depends on outer terminal; portable but requires config tuning |
| **OSC 52 clipboard** | `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features` | **MEDIUM** | SSH-friendly; most modern terminals support it |
| **Escape-time** | `set escape-time 0` | **LOW** | Straightforward; most multiplexers have equivalent |
| **List-sessions / list-windows** | Query API (`tmux list-*`) | **MEDIUM-HIGH** | Python capture scripts depend on this; herdr would need equivalent JSON API |
| **Popup menus** | `display-menu` + `display-popup` | **MEDIUM** | Requires custom implementation; herdr's popup system must fit terminal height |
| **Mouse event bindings** | `MouseDown3Pane`, `MouseDragEnd1Pane`, `DoubleClick1Pane` | **MEDIUM** | Most multiplexers support mouse; behavior may differ |
| **Pane/window flags** | `#{window_flags}`, `#{pane_mode}`, `#{pane_tty}` | **HIGH** | Direct tmux introspection; herdr query API must expose equivalent |
| **Process detection (vim heuristic)** | `ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}'` | **LOW** | Portable; herdr must expose per-pane TTY for this to work |

**Critical blocker for direct porting:** The workmux status integration fundamentally relies on tmux's per-window user-option storage (`@<name>_status`) + format-string interpolation (`#{@option}`). Without this, the entire 🤖/💬/✅ icon system collapses. **Workaround:** Implement a herdr-native status storage layer (file-based, database, or socket IPC) and rewrite the status display hook to use herdr's equivalent of window-status-format.

| **6. Zsh/shell convenience** | `dot_config/shell/38_workmux.sh:39-73` | `wmclear [N]` / `wmclear --all` function; `wmsb` alias for sidebar daemon |

**Tmux-specific dependencies (hard to port):**
- **Per-window user-options** (`@workmux_status`): workmux uses `tmux set-option -w '@workmux_status' &lt;state&gt;` to store state persistently in window options
- **Window-status format substitution** (`#{@workmux_status}`): tmux's format string engine reads the user-option and inlines it into window tabs
- **Catppuccin theme plugin** (`run ~/.tmux/plugins/tmux/catppuccin.tmux`): theme sets the base window-text format; our overlay appends the user-option
- **Sticky state semantics**: `working` state never auto-clears on focus (by design) — requires explicit hook calls to `set-window-status done`

**Portability to "herdr":** Medium-high difficulty. "herdr" would need:
- Equivalent per-pane/window user-option storage mechanism
- Format-string interpolation in its status bar
- The same hook-firing integration points

### 4. NEOVIM EXPERIENCE

**Distribution:** LazyVim (explicit `require("config.lazy")` in `init.lua`, bootstrapping `folke/lazy.nvim` + LazyVim plugins)

**Key files:**

- `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua` — system clipboard + SSH-conditional OSC52

**Clipboard/OSC52 handling (SSH-conditional):**
```lua
-- dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua:12-19
if vim.env.SSH_CONNECTION or vim.env.SSH_TTY then
  local osc52 = require("vim.ui.clipboard.osc52")
  vim.g.clipboard = {
    name = "OSC 52",
    copy = { ["+"] = osc52.copy("+"), ["*"] = osc52.copy("*") },
    paste = { ["+"] = osc52.paste("+"), ["*"] = osc52.paste("*") },
  }
end
```
Routes `+`/`*` registers through OSC 52 over SSH; locally uses LazyVim's default (pbcopy/xclip on macOS/Linux).

**Tmux-nvim integration:** `vim-tmux-navigator` plugin
- File: `dot_config/nvim/lua/exact_plugins/vim-tmux-navigator.lua`
- Plugin: `christoomey/vim-tmux-navigator` (official)
- Bindings: `&lt;C-h/j/k/l&gt;` → `TmuxNavigate{Left,Down,Up,Right}`
- **Pairs with tmux keybindings:** `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf.tmpl:232-236` has the `is_vim` heuristic that forwards the keys to nvim or calls `select-pane`
- Detects vim/nvim via: `ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}' | grep -iqE '^[^TXZ ]+ +(\\S+\\/)?g?\\.?(view|n?vim?x?)(-wrapped)?(diff)?$'`

## SUMMARY: TMUX DEPENDENCIES FOR HERDR MIGRATION

| Feature | Tmux API Used | Portability Risk | Notes |
|---------|---------------|------------------|-------|
| **Per-window user-options** | `tmux set-option -w '@&lt;name&gt;'` | **HIGH** | No equivalent in most multiplexers; requires custom state storage |
| **Format-string interpolation** | `#{@option}`, `#{?@option, ...}` | **HIGH** | Powerful but tmux-specific; alternatives may not have equivalent |
| **Window-status format** | `set window-status-format` + `#{window_name}` + custom vars | **HIGH** | Theme plugin architecture is tmux-specific |
| **Copy-mode tables** | `copy-mode-vi` vs `copy-mode` + `send-keys -X` | **MEDIUM** | Selectable copy modes exist; actions are portable (vi/emacs) |
| **Mode-keys setting** | `set mode-keys vi|emacs` | **MEDIUM** | Most multiplexers support both; switching is straightforward |
| **Extended keys (CSI-u)** | `set extended-keys on` + `terminal-features` | **MEDIUM** | Depends on outer terminal; portable but requires config tuning |
| **OSC 52 clipboard** | `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features` | **MEDIUM** | SSH-friendly; most modern terminals support it |
| **Escape-time** | `set escape-time 0` | **LOW** | Straightforward; most multiplexers have equivalent |
| **List-sessions / list-windows** | Query API (`tmux list-*`) | **MEDIUM-HIGH** | Python capture scripts depend on this; herdr would need equivalent JSON API |
| **Popup menus** | `display-menu` + `display-popup` | **MEDIUM** | Requires custom implementation; herdr's popup system must fit terminal height |
| **Mouse event bindings** | `MouseDown3Pane`, `MouseDragEnd1Pane`, `DoubleClick1Pane` | **MEDIUM** | Most multiplexers support mouse; behavior may differ |
| **Pane/window flags** | `#{window_flags}`, `#{pane_mode}`, `#{pane_tty}` | **HIGH** | Direct tmux introspection; herdr query API must expose equivalent |
| **Process detection (vim heuristic)** | `ps -o state= -o comm= -t '#{pane_tty}'` | **LOW** | Portable; herdr must expose per-pane TTY for this to work |

**Critical blocker for direct porting:** The workmux status integration fundamentally relies on tmux's per-window user-option storage (`@&lt;name&gt;_status`) + format-string interpolation (`#{@option}`). Without this, the entire 🤖/💬/✅ icon system collapses. **Workaround:** Implement a herdr-native status storage layer (file-based, database, or socket IPC) and rewrite the status display hook to use herdr's equivalent of window-status-format.</result>

### 5. GENERAL TMUX SETTINGS (common.conf.tmpl)

| Setting | Value | Purpose |
|---------|-------|---------|
| `escape-time` | 0 | No ESC delay (Neovim, coding agents) |
| `mouse` | on | Mouse support (right-click menus, drag-select) |
| `mode-keys` | vi (if enableVimMode) | vi mode in copy mode; else emacs |

| `renumber-windows` | on | Auto-close gaps when windows killed |
| `focus-events` | on | Vim autoread compatibility |
| `detach-on-destroy` | off | Switch to another session instead of detaching when current is closed |
| `status` | on | Status bar visible |
| `monitor-activity` | on | Activity flag in tab (#) |
